title: Une application soutenue par l'IA vient en aide aux directions d'écoles : "Plus de 3.200 autorisations ont déjà été accordées"
content:
Une application soutenue par l'IA vient en aide aux directions d'écoles : "Plus de 3.200 autorisations ont déjà été accordées"
La Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles a lancé "mAGEordome", une application propulsée par l'intelligence artificielle pour aider les directions d'écoles à décrypter et gérer le flux annuel des circulaires administratives.
- Publié le 24-09-2026 à 16h51
Une application est désormais disponible pour les directions d'écoles et le personnel administratif, pour les guider dans le foisonnement de circulaires concernant l'enseignement. "mAGEordome", tel est le nom de l'outil, utilise aussi l'intelligence artificielle pour tenter de simplifier la vie des écoles.
Avec l'aide de l'IA, il est possible de rechercher une information dans les textes, d'obtenir le résumé d'une circulaire, d'en extraire les nouveautés avec les échéances à respecter, ou encore de poser des questions concernant le contenu.
L'administration générale de l'enseignement (AGE) de la Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles le communique jeudi. "Plus de 3.200 autorisations d'accès ont déjà été accordées", précise l'administration. Les retours sont encouragés, pour faire évoluer l'application en fonction des besoins concrets.
Une centaine de circulaires environ est publiée chaque année à destination des différents réseaux et niveaux d'enseignement, avec des informations concrètes sur le fonctionnement des écoles, etc. mAGEordome recueille les circulaires publiées depuis le 1er janvier 2020.
L'application "propose aussi un calendrier regroupant les tâches et les échéances", de quoi aider les directions au quotidien.

title: Genomic Research as a Critical Pathway to Diagnosis for Individuals with Rare Disease
content: Many individuals with rare monogenic disease remain molecularly undiagnosed due to challenges accessing genetic testing, ambiguity in interpretation of uncertain variants, and latency between novel disease-gene discovery and adoption into clinical pipelines. The Rare Genomes Project (RGP) provides a remote, research-based genomic sequencing (GS) service for rare disease families to overcome diagnostic barriers while advancing the understanding of the genetic basis of rare disease. Short-read GS and family-centered analysis were performed to identify causes of primary disease. Variants meeting return criteria were clinically confirmed and returned to families. Since 2017, RGP enrolled clinically heterogeneous, undiagnosed rare disease families from all fifty states, Washington DC, and Puerto Rico. Findings were returned to 272 of 1014 sequenced families, resulting in a solve rate of 23.3% and a returned strong candidate rate of 3.5%. Condition-specific return rates ranged from 15% to 40% with many families receiving a result in a known disease gene after healthcare access challenges. Research interventions contributed to returns in 16% of all families and included variants in recently discovered or non-coding disease genes, additional functional studies to resolve variant uncertainty, and real-time data sharing to empower novel disease-gene discovery. RGP demonstrates that a research-based, patient-driven remote sequencing study can effectively bridge a diagnostic gap for rare disease families underserved in current clinical care. This study also underscores the clinical utility of GS with frequent re-analysis and highlights the critical continued role of research in variant interpretation, method innovation, and genomic knowledge base expansion for rare disease diagnosis.

title: Proefproject Bilzen toont: "Mobiliteitsarmoede oplossen vraagt meer dan enkel deelwagen en -fiets"
content:
Mobiliteitsarmoede kan je niet oplossen met een deelwagen en deelfiets. Dat blijkt uit een proefproject in de sociale woonwijk Bivelenhof in Bilzen-Hoeselt. Bewoners moesten intensief begeleid worden, vooraleer ze gebruik maakten van het aanbod, en hadden ook interesse in andere vervoersmiddelen zoals een driewieler en een scootmobiel.
Proefproject Bilzen toont: "Mobiliteitsarmoede oplossen vraagt meer dan enkel deelwagen en -fiets"
De voorbije jaren is het aanbod aan deelwagens en -fietsen ook in Limburg sterk uitgebreid. Maar uit een rondvraag in de sociale woonwijk in Sledderlo (Genk) merkte de sociale organisatie SAAMO Limburg dat veel bewoners dat aanbod helemaal niet kenden.
Bewoners die wel op de hoogte waren van het aanbod, maakten er geen gebruik van omdat ze niet goed begrepen hoe het systeem werkte, hoe ze het digitaal konden boeken of wat het precies zou kosten.
SAAMO Limburg en de sociale huisvestingsmaatschappij Wonen in Limburg zijn daarop in het voorjaar met een proefproject gestart in de wijk Bivelenhof in Bilzen, om na te gaan hoe ze mobiliteitsarmoede tegen kunnen gaan. Bewoners konden er gebruik maken van een deelauto.
Mobiliteitsoplossingen moeten vertrekken vanuit de concrete noden van bewoners
Emma Reymer, buurtopbouwwerker SAAMO Limburg.
"De belangrijkste conclusie van het project is dat inclusieve deelmobiliteit meer vraagt dan het plaatsen van een voertuig in een wijk. Dus hebben we in Bivelenhof ook voor een elektrische fiets, een elektrische driewieler en een scootmobiel gezorgd", vertelt buurtopbouwwerker Emma Reymer van SAAMO.
"Een standaardaanpak volstaat niet: mobiliteitsoplossingen moeten vertrekken vanuit de concrete noden van bewoners, niet omgekeerd."
Eigen wagen
Reymer merkte ook wat weerstand bij de bewoners. "Mensen laten hun auto niet graag los. Ze vinden: mijn auto is mijn vrijheid. Maar met dit project hebben we ook kunnen aantonen dat een auto soms hun vrijheid net belemmert. En dat ze ook veel hebben aan een fiets of een deelwagen."
SAAMO Limburg roept gemeentebesturen intussen op om aandacht te hebben voor de noden van bewoners. "Basisbereikbaarheid blijft het belangrijkste. Degelijk openbaar vervoer blijft de basis. Deelmobiliteit kan alleen een aanvulling zijn", klinkt het beslist.
Aanbevelingen
Mobilize Share, het bedrijf achter de deelwagen, wil er bij nieuwe initiatieven alvast rekening mee houden. "De ervaringen tonen hoe belangrijk het is om deelmobiliteit lokaal te verankeren en gebruikers voldoende ondersteuning te bieden. Door samen te werken met organisaties zoals SAAMO Limburg leren we hoe we ons aanbod nog beter kunnen laten aansluiten bij verschillende gebruikers."
"De resultaten van dit pilootproject bevestigen hoe belangrijk samenwerking is. Door bewoners, sociale organisaties, lokale besturen en mobiliteitsaanbieders rond de tafel te brengen, ontstaan oplossingen die aansluiten bij de noden van mensen", vult Reinout Van Der Sijpe van Wonen in Limburg aan. "Als sociale woonmaatschappij zetten we samen met onze partners in op betaalbaar wonen én leefbare buurten, waarin ook duurzame en inclusieve mobiliteit een belangrijke plaats inneemt."
De deelwagen in Bivelenhof was de eerste in een sociale woonwijk in Bilzen-Hoeselt en blijft na het pilootproject in gebruik. De stad wil op termijn nog meer deelwagens aanbieden op haar grondgebied. "Ik ben dankbaar dat SAAMO onze stad uitkoos voor dit project. Net de meest kwetsbaren in onze maatschappij hebben het meest baat bij een uitgebreid aanbod aan deelmobiliteit", besluit schepen van Mobiliteit Yves Croux (Team Burgemeester).

title: Fußball spielender Pfarrer: Der Elfmeterheld mit Verbindung nach ganz oben
content:
Johann Wurzer ist Pfarrer in der österreichischen Gemeinde Opponitz – und spielt in seiner Freizeit leidenschaftlich Fußball. Als kürzlich der Torhüter beim SV Opponitz ausgefallen ist, half der 64 Jahre alte Wurzer aus. Ein echter Glücksfall für den Verein, denn er hielt einen Elfmeter und verhalf der Reserve des SV Opponitz zum Auswärtssieg gegen den des FCU Strengberg in der Liga. Ein Anruf bei einem Priester, der von Berufs wegen auch bei internationalen Turnieren antritt.
SZ: Herr Wurzer, wann haben Sie erfahren, dass Sie von der Kirche ins Fußballtor wechseln sollen?
Johann Wurzer: Der Trainer hat mich am Abend vor dem Spiel gefragt. Beim Training. Ich bin ja kein Stammspieler beim SV Opponitz, trainiere aber regelmäßig mit der Mannschaft.
Was war Ihre erste Reaktion?
Innere Freude darüber, dass ich in meinem Alter überhaupt bei Spielen mitwirken kann.
Mit ihren 64 Jahren sind sie wohl sehr fit.
Zur Fußball-Weltmeisterschaft haben wir eine Messe veranstaltet. Das ist für mich als Fußballer Pflicht. Im Anschluss durften die Gottesdienstteilnehmer ins Elfmeterschießen gegen mich. 67 Leute sind angetreten, da bin ich ungefähr 140 Mal auf den Boden geflogen.
Den Körpereinsatz haben Sie auch beim Spiel gegen den SV Strengberg gezeigt. Zwischenzeitlich führte Ihre Mannschaft mit 3:1. Als der Schiedsrichter einen Elfmeter für die Gegner gepfiffen hat, haben Sie da gebetet?
Nein, ich habe den Elfmeterschützen genau beobachtet. Er hat ins linke Eck geschaut und die rechte Hand beim Ablegen vorn gehabt. Das hieß für mich, er möchte in diese Ecke schießen. Zweimal hat er dieses ziemlich eindeutige Zeichen gemacht. Ich hatte recht.
War Ihnen dabei auch Ihre innere Verbindung nach ganz oben hilfreich?
Ich würde eher sagen, das ist die Routine, wenn man über 50 Jahre Torwart ist.
Sie haben den Elfer gehalten, sodass Ihre Mannschaft am Ende das Spiel gewonnen hat.
Eine Sensation! Wir haben eineinhalb Jahre nicht mehr mit der Reserve gewonnen. Das haben wir auch gefeiert und da habe ich auch wohl einen guten Teil von dem gesponserten Bier mitgetrunken.
Aber hoffentlich nicht zu viel, Sie mussten ja am Wochenende noch arbeiten.
Ich musste am folgenden Tag erst am Abend die Samstagsmesse halten. Da hatte ich noch ein bisschen Zeit, mich von der Siegesfeier zu erholen.
Nebenbei spielen Sie auch für die Priesternationalmannschaft in Österreich.
Ja, es gibt jedes Jahr Europameisterschaften, da nehmen meistens 18 Mannschaften teil. Die nächste ist in Priština, in Kosovo. Und jeder muss halt schauen, dass er sich bis dahin fit hält.
Wie schlagen sich denn die österreichischen Pfarrer dabei?
Ich sage immer, wir sind ziemlich die Besten vom letzten Drittel. Polen, Kroatien und Portugal machen seit Jahren den Sieg unter sich aus.
Woran liegt das, weniger Sünden?
In Polen finden zum Beispiel in einem Jahr so viele Priesterweihen statt wie in Österreich in zehn Jahren. Die könnten wahrscheinlich jedes Jahr eine neue Mannschaft aufstellen.
Spielen Priester eigentlich fairer als andere Fußballer?
Nein, sie werden von genau so viel Ehrgeiz und der Fanatismus angetrieben wie andere Sportler. Da wird ebenso psychologisch gearbeitet und optimiert.
Was ist für Sie eigentlich schwieriger: Einen Elfmeter zu halten oder genügend Besucher in die Kirche zu locken?
Eine volle Kirche. Ich betreue drei Pfarreien. In einer davon kommen sehr viele junge Familien und Jugendliche in die Kirche. In den anderen beiden eher nicht. Woran das liegt, weiß ich leider auch nicht.
Jetzt, wo Sie so bekannt sind, kommen vielleicht wieder mehr Menschen?
Vielleicht. Das wäre schön.

title: Krkobabić: U jednu ulicu u Željuši, do juče zapuštenu, uselilo se 10 porodica
content:
EMIL VAS / BETAPHOTO Krkobabić: U jednu ulicu u Željuši, do juče zapuštenu, uselilo se 10 porodica autor: Beta Politika 18. sep. 2026. 17:53 0 Podeli vest: Postavi Nova.rs za omiljeni Google izvor Više Ministar za brigu o selu Milan Krkobabić ocenio je danas da se značaj državne podrške vidi po naseljenoj ulici u selu Željuša u Dimitrovgradu, obnovljenom Domu kulture punom posetilaca i kroz subvencije stolaru da kupi mašinu i proširi posao. Podeli vest: Oglas "Кada vidimo da se u jednu ulicu u Željuši, do juče zapuštenu, uselilo 10 porodica, da jedan stolar u selu zahvaljujući podršci Ministarstva može da kupi mašinu i proširi posao, a da se obnovljeni seoski Dom kulture ponovo puni ljudima, onda vidimo šta znači kada državna podrška stigne tamo gde je najpotrebnija", rekao je Krkobabić tokom posete Dimitrovgradu i njegovim selima, gde se sastao sa meštanima i predstavnicima lokalne samouprave. Podrška Dimitrovgradu prethodnih godina stizala je kroz različite programe Ministarstva za brigu o selu, a rezultati tih ulaganja se vide kroz konkretne ljude i njihove priče, piše u saopštenju Ministarstva. Ministar je posetio stolarsku radionicu Dimitra Dimitrijeva iz Gradinja koji je zahvaljujući Programu podrške razvoju privrednih aktivnosti u seoskim sredinama, dobijenim sredstvima kupio mašinu za sečenje PVC profila, vrednu 1,6 miliona dinara i unapredio proizvodnju. Navedeno je da Dimitrijev, sa još trojicom majstora, ima puno posla, a da mu dodatni angažman obezbeđuje učešće u programu energetske sanacije domaćinstava, u okviru kojeg izrađuju i ugrađuju novu stolariju. "Sa novom mašinom, posao završavamo znatno brže. Planirao sam da je kupim odavno, ali nisam imao dovoljno novca, pa je podrška Ministarstva stigla u pravom trenutku, jer sada možemo mnogo više posla da prihvatimo", rekao je Dimitrijev. U Dimitrovgradu je do sada dodeljeno 39 seoskih kuća sa okućnicom, a posebno se izdvojila Željuša, u kojoj je "jedna ulica, do juče gotovo zamrla, ponovo dobila svoje stanovnike". Zajedno sa susednom Lukavicom, ta dva sela dobila su 25 novih domaćinstava i obnovljeni Dom kulture u Lukavici, u koji je kroz Program Ministarstva za brigu o selu uloženo gotovo tri miliona dinara. "Dom je kompletno obnovljen, od podova, preko fasade, do nameštaja i računarske opreme. Imamo nove stolove za bilijar, društvene igre i prostor u kojem penzioneri mogu da se okupe i druže, ali i gde mladi provode vreme i deca iz Dimitrovgrada dolaze ovde. Ranije je Dom radio, ali nismo imali ovakav život u njemu. Sada je to ponovo mesto koje okupljanja svih generacija", rekla je dugogodišnja predsednica Mesne zajednice Lukavica Danka Dimitrov. Dimitrovgradu je u prethodnom periodu dodeljen i minibus za prevoz seoskog stanovništva, podržan je razvoj zadrugarstva, a šesti Miholjski susreti u tom gradu biće održani u nedelju u selu Smilovci. Ta manifestacija okuplja meštane različitih generacija, čuva tradiciju i običaje ovog kraja i predstavlja priliku da se sela Dimitrovgrada predstave kroz kulturu, sport, stare zanate i tradicionalne vrednosti, piše u saopštenju Ministarstva. milan krkobabić Pratite nas na društvenim mrežama: Koje je tvoje mišljenje o ovoj temi? title: FN-organisation: Færre migranter ankommer til Europa ad søvejen
content:
Siden årets første dag og til nu er omkring 60.000 migranter og flygtninge ankommet til Europa ad søvejen.
Det er omkring 38.000 færre end i samme periode sidste år, oplyser FN's migrationsorgan, IOM, ifølge Reuters.
Til gengæld har der været en stigning i antallet af omkomne migranter og flygtninge til søs, da rejserne ofte foretages i ikke-sødygtige, overfyldte både fra Libyens kyst, skriver nyhedsbureauet.
Knap 2.300 personer er indtil videre meldt omkommet eller savnet i år, hvilket er knap 300 flere end sidste år.

title: DEFYING GRAVITY: Young SA gymnast has turned self-doubt into a winning routine
content:
For the 2026 Commonwealth Games, only six spots were allocated to South Africa in gymnastics. Because the women’s team had been so successful in 2022, finishing fourth, the decision was to send a full women’s team again this year. That left just one place open for the men. Determined to claim this spot was 20-year-old Daniel Mclean.
After an impressive showing at the 2026 African Artistic Gymnastics Championships in Cameroon earlier this year, where he won his first continental title, Mclean had an inkling the spot might be his. But with several talented young gymnasts vying for the same opportunity, he was careful not to get ahead of himself. Nevertheless, he continued to prepare as he awaited the decision of the South African Sports Confederation and Olympic Committee (Sascoc).
A month before the Commonwealth Games, Mclean was informed that he had secured the final place on Team South Africa. A wave of relief washed over him. It would be his Commonwealth Games debut and, heading into the competition, all he wanted to do was absorb the experience.
“It was exciting,” he said. “I just wanted to soak up the experience and enjoy it. I didn’t really set high expectations in terms of placings.”
But then he delivered an outstanding qualification floor routine, topping his subdivision and qualifying fourth for the final. Competing against Olympic and World Championship athletes such as England’s Luke Whitehouse and Canada’s René Cournoyer, Mclean held his own on one of the biggest stages of his career so far. Executing a clean, high-pressure routine, he announced himself on the international stage by finishing fifth overall on the floor.
“I was not stressed, just nervous. But it was a different type of nervous for me compared with African champs or nationals,” Mclean said. “It was just the environment. The crowd was huge; they were loud and encouraging, and it was different. But it was a good different.”
Although his Commonwealth Games performance announced his arrival internationally, it was his African Championship gold that secured qualification for his debut World Championships coming up in October in Rotterdam.
‘Obsessed with gymnastics’
Mclean has been training at the same club in Roodepoort, Vision Gymnastics, since he was five-years-old. His older sister, Phoebe, was the one who initially received a free trial lesson at the gym.
“Everything she wanted to do, I wanted to do,” he said. “My mom claims that I was crying and said that I also wanted to do it.”
Eventually, Mclean got his own trial lesson and promptly joined the gym. It was not long before he was selected to join the high-performance programme, said his longtime coach Kevin Basson.
“He was quite flexible and just performed above the rest in his class,” Basson said. “It was only around 11 or 12-years-old that we could see this kid can truly make a difference.”
Mclean attended Cliffview Primary and later Reddford House Northcliff, all the while juggling the demands of elite gymnastics. At times, he faced bullying for pursuing a sport that did not fit traditional perceptions of masculinity, he said.
According to Basson, however, Mclean’s love for gymnastics is what sets him apart. “He is obsessed with gymnastics. We have gymnastics trivia days, and he can name all the athletes, men or women, what year they performed and where. He is just so engaged and involved in gymnastics that it is a part of him and who he is.
“That, and the morals and values he has, are what truly make him great at this
sport. He is hard-working and diligent, and takes pride in performing with clean lines,” added Basson.
Mclean is completing a BCom degree in transport and logistics management at the University of Johannesburg. “My parents have been the most supportive people in my life, emotionally and financially,” he said. “They’ve just been there for me through everything, and I can’t thank them enough for the support they constantly gave me.”
His biggest influence, though, has been Basson, with whom he has worked for more than a decade. “It’s just his way of looking at things and his positivity and his way of pushing always,” said Mclean.
Basson said he was “proud and honoured” that Mclean chose him as his coach. “We work as a team and truly trust each other. We often talk about what works and what doesn’t, and essentially work alongside each other to achieve the goals, and it’s not just me telling him what to do. It’s a partnership.”
Life’s little lessons
As with anything in life, Mclean’s gymnastics journey has not been without its obstacles. There were moments when he felt uncertain about his abilities and his future in the sport.
In 2019, when he was about 14-years-old, Mclean was set to compete in the Olympic Hopes Cup in the Czech Republic. It was his debut on the junior international stage. At the time, however, the pressure was so overwhelming that he did not want to continue. “I was just going through a stage where I felt too much stress and I just... I didn’t know what to do,” he said.
It was during moments like those that Basson reminded him of how far he had come and what more he still could do. “If it wasn’t for him, I don’t think I would have continued,” said Mclean.
There have also been periods of instability and self-doubt, particularly when trying to balance academics and gymnastics. “In first year [of university], I struggled a bit mentally with balancing university work and gym because I am a perfectionist, so I like to do well in both. But I reminded myself why I’m here in gymnastics and when I adopted a more positive attitude, I was able to get that balance back again.”
Although he did not do as well as expected at the Olympic Hopes Cup, the setback taught him about perspective. “I learnt that we’re all human, that it’s okay to not have a good day. It’s part of the sport,” he said. “Also, watching top gymnasts make mistakes and still enjoy what they’re doing helped me realise this.”
The Commonwealth Games further reinforced Mclean’s belief that, despite the self-doubt and uncertainty, he is capable and belongs among the world’s top athletes. “And it’s just a fraction of what I can accomplish, and I can reach those other goals,” he said.
As a result of all his hard work, one of his goals, to compete at a senior World Championships, will be coming true in October. Beyond that, Mclean has his eyes set on the 2028 Los Angeles Olympic Games. DM

title: Perceived faith-oriented public-space environments, activity participation, and social connectedness among older adults in Quanzhou Ancient City
content: Older adults’ perceptions of urban public spaces are associated with their outdoor activities and social interactions, whereas locally embedded folk culture is associated with distinctive patterns of spatial engagement. In the context of historic city renewal, understanding how culturally embedded environments are associated with social connectedness among older adults is essential. This study examines how environmental perceptions of public spaces are associated with social connectedness among older adults and tests the indirect associations through activity participation. Using Licheng District of Quanzhou Ancient City as the study area, a structural equation model was developed to analyze the path relationships among five dimensions of environmental perception—activity-oriented, landscape-oriented, accessibility-oriented, communicative, and faith-oriented elements—activity participation, and social connectedness. Data were obtained from two repeated cross-sectional surveys conducted in October 2020 and January 2024 (n = 620) and analyzed using structural equation modeling. After adjustment for gender, age, educational attainment, household composition, and religious affiliation, all five dimensions of environmental perception were positively associated with stronger social connectedness: activity-oriented (β = 0.100, p = 0.017), landscape-oriented (β = 0.157, p < 0.001), accessibility-oriented (β = 0.169, p < 0.001), communicative (β = 0.125, p = 0.001), and faith-oriented perception (β = 0.091, p = 0.022). Faith-based folk activities (β = 0.169), non-faith folk activities (β = 0.145), and non-folk activities (β = 0.180) were also positively associated with social connectedness (all p < 0.001). Bootstrap analyses identified activity-specific indirect associations between environmental perception and social connectedness. Given the repeated cross-sectional design, the findings indicate statistical associations rather than causal effects.

title: Med 44 milijoni darovalcev niso našli ustreznega, nakar mu je drugo življenje dala hči
content:
»Velik šok je bila ugotovitev, da v svetovnem registru, v katerem je 44 milijonov darovalcev, ni primernega darovalca zame,« je razložil Marko, ki je spomladi izvedel, da ima eno od oblik levkemije. »Nisem vedel, kdaj se bo bolezen poslabšala, nisem vedel, koliko časa imam še na razpolago,« je ob letošnjem svetovnem dnevu darovalcev krvotvornih matičnih celic svojo zgodbo predstavil Marko, ki se je nato uspešno zdravil s presaditvijo krvotvornih matičnih celic.
Darovalca matičnih celic so zdravniki iskali v domačem registru darovalcev matičnih celic Slovenija Donor, v katerega je zdaj vključenih 25.520 ljudi. A nihče ni bil primeren. Tako kot niso našli darovalca v svetovnem registru, ki ima 44 milijonov darovalcev.
Takrat se je v zgodbo vključila žena Marjeta, ki je spomladi spodbudila vseslovensko akcijo novih vpisov v register Slovenija Donor. Zaradi njene odločenosti, da ne bodo samo čakali, sta se v register vpisala več kot 1602 nova potencialna darovalca, ki so se jim – tako kot vsem drugim potencialnim darovalcem – javno zahvalili. »Ko so ljudje izvedeli, da postopek darovanja matičnih celic ni boleč in zapleten, so se odločili za ta korak. Vendar primernega darovalca za Marka še vedno ni bilo,« je povedala Marjeta. Potem so ugotovili, da je primeren darovalec njuna hči Zala, ki je očetu dobesedno »dala drugo življenje«.
»Od priprav na postopek do postopka darovanja matičnih celic so me vseskozi preverjali, kako sem, ali mi je udobno, tako da je bilo vse skupaj mačji kašelj,« je razložila Zala, ki je zadovoljna, da je lahko pomagala očetu oziroma da je pomagala sočloveku. Zdravnik Primož Poženel, medicinski vodja registra Slovenija Donor, je poudaril, da je darovanje matičnih celic varno in poteka pod medicinskim nadzorom. Darovalec pred postopkom jemlje zdravila pet dni, potem pa mu v peturnem postopku iz krvi odvzamejo matične celice – oziroma kri obdelajo pozneje –, tako da je postopek preprost in varen za telo.
Ima pa telo oziroma kostni mozeg neverjetno sposobnost, da v kratkem nadomesti odvzete matične celice. »Pri postopku je bistveno, da darovalec ne škodi sebi in bolniku, zato tudi dobro preverimo, ali je zdrav,« je dejal Poženel. Poleg tega vse poteka pod zdravniškim nadzorom in pozneje spremljajo tudi darovalca.
Ob letošnjem svetovnem dnevu darovalcev, ko s sloganom Daj se na seznam vabijo k vpisu v register darovalcev krvotvornih matičnih celic, so poudarili, da je ta postopek zdravljenja krvnega raka sodobnejši način zdravljenja od presajanja kostnega mozga, ki v očeh javnosti velja za boleč postopek. Klasični postopek uporabijo v enem od 40 primerov zdravljenja na leto, je pojasnila hematologinja Polona Novak s kliničnega oddelka za hematologijo pri UKC Ljubljana. »S tem zdravljenjem človek dobi nov imunski sistem. To je prva imunoterapija, ki učinkuje. Je pa pogoj, da najdemo darovalca. V 99 odstotkih nam ga uspe najti.«
Pri iskanju darovalca ni pomembna krvna skupina, ampak človeški levkocitni antigeni oziroma HLA, ki so skupek beljakovin na površini celic, ki pomagajo imunskemu sistemu prepoznati lastne celice in napasti tuje vsiljivce. Lastnosti oziroma značilni tipi HLA se razlikujejo od območja do območja, zato je pomemben slovenski register.
»Vsako leto iz našega registra izbrišemo okoli petsto darovalcev zaradi starosti, a je pomembno, da bazo obnavljamo. Zato vabimo ljudi, stare od 18 do 40 let, da se prijavijo v naš register potencialnih darovalcev krvotvornih matičnih celic,« je poudarila Sendi Montanič, vodja registra Slovenija Donor. Uspešnost zdravljenja je povezana tudi s starostjo darovalca, saj je uspešnost večja, če je darovalec mlajši. Je pa običajno, da iščejo darovalce znotraj družine – v 25 odstotkih je to sorojenec –, potem v slovenskem registru, v katerem je podobnost znotraj populacije večja, nato pa še v svetovni bazi 44 milijonov ljudi. Postopek je seveda bistveno hitrejši, če je darovalec iz Slovenije.

title: L’Azerbaïdjan gracie le Français emprisonné Martin Ryan, par décret présidentiel
content:
20 Minutes avec AFP
Un nouveau succès pour la diplomatie française. L’Azerbaïdjan a gracié ce mercredi Martin Ryan, un Français emprisonné dans ce pays du Caucase depuis fin 2023.
La décision intervient quelques heures après la levée des sanctions européennes visant l’oligarque russe Alicher Ousmanov que demandait la France.
Selon un décret du président azerbaïdjanais Ilham Aliev publié mercredi, Martin Ryan figure dans une liste de 20 personnes graciées et est le seul ressortissant français à en bénéficier.
Un accord de libération
Selon un diplomate à Bruxelles, Paris a fait pression auprès des pays membres de l’UE pour lever les sanctions visant Alicher Ousmanov dans le cadre d’un accord de libération de prisonniers impliquant des citoyens français détenus en Azerbaïdjan. La France n’a jamais confirmé de telles tractations, mais réclame depuis des mois la libération de l’homme d’affaires Martin Ryan, condamné à dix ans de prison pour « espionnage » en mars 2026.
Installé à Bakou depuis plusieurs années, Martin Ryan avait été arrêté le 4 décembre 2023 par les autorités azerbaïdjanaises, l’accusant d' « espionnage » au profit des services secrets français. Le ministère français des Affaires étrangères a toujours rejeté « catégoriquement » ces accusations, qualifiant cette détention d'« arbitraire ».
Un autre Français encore emprisonné
Selon l’accusation, Martin Ryan aurait collecté des informations concernant les relations de l’Azerbaïdjan avec la Turquie, l’Iran et le Pakistan, concernant des entreprises liées à la Russie et à la Chine et sur des questions stratégiques régionales liées au Karabakh. Son procès avait débuté en janvier 2025 à Bakou mais ce n’est que plus d’un an plus tard, le 16 mars dernier, qu’il avait été condamné. Un coaccusé azerbaïdjanais, Azad Mamedli, avait été, lui, condamné à douze ans de prison pour « haute trahison ».
Selon le décret présidentiel publié mercredi, outre Martin Ryan, quatre autres ressortissants étrangers figurent parmi les personnes libérées : un Russe, un Pakistanais et deux Turcs. Un autre citoyen français est emprisonné en Azerbaïdjan, l’homme d’affaires Anass Derraz. Il a été condamné à douze ans de prison en novembre 2025 à Bakou dans une affaire où il est accusé d’avoir accepté un pot-de-vin d’un oligarque russe.
Relations tendues
Les relations bilatérales entre la France et l’Azerbaïdjan se sont fortement dégradées après la reprise par Bakou, en septembre 2023, du contrôle du territoire du Karabakh, alors à majorité arménienne, ce qui a provoqué le déplacement de plus de 100.000 habitants.
Bakou reprochait le soutien de Paris à l’Arménie. Les autorités françaises ont accusé en retour l’Azerbaïdjan d’une ingérence concernant ses territoires d’outre-mer, ce que Bakou nie.

title: Houston now requires air conditioning in all rentals, making cooling a housing standard
content:
In one of Texas' hottest major cities, air conditioning is no longer an optional perk for renters.
Houston City Council voted to require landlords to provide cooling in every rental unit, making AC a basic housing standard.
Here's what to know
Landlords now have 120 days — until December — to equip every rental unit with some form of cooling, according to the Houston Chronicle, whether it be central air, a window AC, or a portable unit.
Council approved the ordinance 12-2, ending Houston's longstanding "window screen exemption." Under that rule, owners could satisfy housing-code standards with screened windows and doors instead of refrigerated air.
In a city where intense summer heat can threaten people's health, that exception became increasingly notable. Going forward, a unit without AC will be handled through the normal code-enforcement system where residents can file a complaint, the health department can inspect the property, and landlords who do not fix the issue can face citations or end up in municipal court.
Backers of the change say it puts Houston in line with other big Texas cities and recognizes cooling as part of a safe, livable home rather than a luxury amenity.
More background
The change comes after several years of record summer heat, coinciding with an increase in heat-related deaths in the Houston area. Indoor cooling can make a major difference for older adults, children, and people with health conditions that get worse in extreme heat.
A 2023 survey put the number of rental households without air conditioning across the Houston metro at 20,400. But that estimate includes homes outside Houston city limits, so not all of those units would be covered by the ordinance.
The Houston fight is also part of a broader Texas debate. State lawmakers tried to create a statewide requirement for air conditioning in rentals, but that effort stalled amid objections to adding more regulations for property owners.
Some Houston officials expressed similar worries. Mayor John Whitmire said he was "fearful" the rule could increase rents and utility bills, while Council Member Twila Carter said, "My concern is for the people that this policy is intended to protect. This comes at a heavy cost, and it will put people on the streets."
What's being done?
Amy Peck, a council member and realtor, said Houston already requires heat even though it had never required air conditioning. She also said renters often had little recourse when an existing AC unit broke and was not repaired.
The ordinance was backed not just by housing advocates but also by the Houston Apartment Association, and there was no apparent landlord opposition during public hearings.
Julia Orduña of Texas Housers explained, "It comes down to that right to choose how much you're going to pay for electricity. It's not about living with or without AC in your unit, it's about deciding when to turn the AC on and off."
Council Member Alejandra Salinas said, "All Houstonians deserve a right to rest from heat, and that's what this ordinance is going to do."

title: Vietnam’s FDI giants race to invest in worker housing
content:
After years of renting outside the company, Nguyen Thi Thanh Tuyen, 36, from Luc Ngan, Bac Ninh province, decided to move into Samsung Display Vietnam's employee dormitory.
FDI giants race to build worker housing
For Tuyen, the dormitory is more than a stable place to live. It also helps cut living costs, allowing her to send more money home to support her two young children.
"I used to rent a room near the company, but the living conditions and security were not as good as at the dormitory. Since moving here, my life has become more stable, and the facilities are well equipped," she said.
"The trade union also gives us gifts and support during holidays and Tet, which gives me peace of mind."
Similarly, Luc Thi Minh, 22, from Ha Quang, Cao Bang province, said that in addition to competitive pay and good benefits, the company provides workers with well-equipped dormitories featuring facilities such as washing machines, a supermarket, gym and hair salon.
"The trade union regularly gives gifts and organizes transportation for workers from remote hometowns like mine to return home during holidays and Tet," she said.
Still, both Tuyen and Minh hope to eventually be able to rent a home long-term or buy a social housing unit at an affordable price so they can feel more secure about staying in their jobs.
Speaking with workers, Hoang Anh Tuan, chairman of the Samsung Display Vietnam trade union, which represents more than 25,000 members, said providing housing is one of the company's key employee welfare policies.
The company has invested in a dormitory with capacity for about 4,500 people, allowing workers to avoid renting accommodation outside the company.
Workers whose hometowns are more than 60 kilometers from the company, as well as those who need accommodation, can stay at the dormitory with low electricity and water costs.
Beyond clean and well-equipped rooms, the facility also has a reading room and English and Korean language classrooms to support workers in their daily jobs.
"The dormitory is not just a place to live. It is also an environment where employees can share, connect and look out for one another, helping them feel secure at work and stay with the company," Tuan said.
Meanwhile, Bui Thi Ngoc Quyen, vice-chairwoman of the Goertek Vietnam trade union, which represents more than 11,000 members, said the union and company work closely to help provide housing for workers, contributing to stable living conditions and uninterrupted production.
In addition to dormitories for new workers, the trade union also serves as a bridge between employees and housing providers, helping workers find suitable accommodation with convenient access to work.
Goertek Vietnam's worker housing facility is expected to open in 2028, providing additional accommodation for employees.
More worker housing on the way
Driven by demand from workers and union members, the Vietnam General Confederation of Labor is developing housing projects that workers can rent.
Three projects have already broken ground in Bac Ninh and Vinh Long, with a combined total of more than 1,700 apartments.
The projects are being accelerated and are expected to open in 2027, helping meet some of the housing needs of workers in industrial parks.
From 2026 to 2030, the confederation plans to invest in 10 to 15 additional projects across the country, with an estimated 9,000 apartments.
The rental housing projects are intended not only to support the government's social housing goals but also to give workers stable accommodation, allowing them to focus on their jobs and stay with companies for longer.
Alongside projects led by the trade union, Bac Ninh, one of northern Vietnam's major industrial hubs, is also stepping up housing development for the 2021-2030 period.
The province aims to complete at least 135,000 social housing units by 2030, in line with a target set by the prime minister, while also focusing on rental housing for low-income residents and industrial workers.
Total investment in housing development during the period is estimated at VND945 trillion (US$36.3 billion).
Bac Ninh has outlined several measures to achieve the goal, including improving policies, planning land reserves, securing funding, streamlining administrative procedures, and developing housing projects and the real estate market.
According to the Vietnam General Confederation of Labor, the trade union has broken ground on rental housing projects for workers in Dong Thap and Bac Ninh and added investment funding plans for projects in Ninh Binh, Da Nang, Quang Ngai and Tay Ninh.
In late September 2025, the confederation held a groundbreaking ceremony for a trade union social housing project in Viet Yen Ward, Bac Ninh, featuring a 10-story building with 477 self-contained rental apartments, elevators, parking and other facilities.
The project is expected to be completed in 2027.
In late August 2026, Standing Deputy Prime Minister Pham Gia Tuc commented on a program to build at least 1 million social housing units for low-income people and industrial workers between 2021 and 2030.
The government's latest policies, particularly those focused on rental housing, aim to meet the growing demand for affordable rentals.
As a result, the targets for social housing development need to be adjusted appropriately, with a stronger focus on rental housing while carefully reviewing the basis, rationale and potential reduction in the overall social housing target.

title: त्रिभुवन र कान्ति राजमार्गमा दुईतर्फी यातायात सञ्चालन
content:
हेटौंडा। हेटौंडाबाट काठमाडौं आवतजावतका लागि प्रयोग हुने त्रिभुवन राजपथ (बाइरोड) र कान्ति राजमार्गमा आजदेखि नियमित रूपमा दुईतर्फी रूपमा सञ्चालनमा आएका छन्।
जिल्ला प्रशासन कार्यालय मकवानपुरका प्रशासकीय अधिकृत सन्तोष सुवेदीले पृथ्वी राजमार्गअन्तर्गत धादिङको कृष्णभीर खण्डमा अवरुद्ध सडक सञ्चालनमा आएसँगै दुबै मार्गमा दुईतर्फी सवारी आवागमन खुला गरिएको जानकारी दिए। त्रिभुवन राजपथले हेटौंडालाई पालुङ–नौबिसे हुँदै काठमाडौंसँग जोड्छ भने कान्ति राजमार्गले हेटौंडालाई टीकाभैरव–ललितपुर हुँदै काठमाडौं उपत्यकासँग जोड्छ।
कृष्णभीरमा सडक अवरुद्ध भएपछि सवारी आवागमनलाई सहज, सुरक्षित तथा व्यवस्थित बनाउन गत भदौ १६ गतेदेखि मालवाहक तथा ठूला यात्रुवाहक सवारीसाधनलाई त्रिभुवन राजपथ हुँदै काठमाडौं जाने र फर्कंदा कान्ति राजमार्ग प्रयोग गर्ने गरी प्रशासनले एकतर्फी व्यवस्था गरेको थियो।
कृष्णभीर खण्डमा सडक सञ्चालनमा आएपछि उक्त व्यवस्था हटाउँदै शुक्रबारदेखि त्रिभुवन राजपथ र कान्ति राजमार्गमा नियमित रूपमा दुईतर्फी रूपमा यातायात सञ्चालन खुला गरिएको प्रशासकीय अधिकृत सुवेदीले बताए।

title: PVR Inox ordered to pay Rs 6,000 after movie show cancelled 10 minutes after start
content:
NEW DELHI: A Hyderabad district consumer commission has directed PVR Inox and an Inox theatre to pay Rs 6,000 to a customer after a movie show was cancelled about 10 minutes after it began. The commission found deficiency in service and unfair trade practice and awarded Rs 5,000 compensation and Rs 1,000 litigation costs. The order was passed on September 11, 2026.
Why did the customer approach the commission?According to the commission order, P Prashanth purchased a ticket for the Telugu film “Hongkong Warriors” for Rs 173 through BookMyShow on January 26, 2025. He reached the theatre on time and started watching the movie, but the show was cancelled about 10 minutes into the screening.
Prashanth alleged that the theatre initially said the show was cancelled because of low occupancy. He said the management later changed its explanation and said there was a technical issue. He claimed the sudden cancellation caused mental distress and inconvenience and that his complaints to BookMyShow and the theatre did not receive a satisfactory response.
He sought Rs 50,000 as compensation for deficiency in service, mental agony and harassment, besides Rs 25,000 towards litigation costs.
The theatre disputed the allegations. It said the show was cancelled because of a technical error caused by storage limitations in the screen's Audi 06. It said its engineering team tried to resolve the issue but could not do so. The theatre also said a 100 percent refund was offered along with an alternative movie experience. It said the refund was later processed and argued that no further compensation was payable.
What did the commission find?The bench of President
Vakkanti Narasimha Rao and member
Suma Vala noted that the theatre had not produced a technical report or other documentary evidence to support its claim that the show was cancelled because of a technical problem.
“The complainant is not in dispute that he arrived at the theatre on time and began watching the movie, however, about 10 minutes into the Screening, the theatre management abruptly cancelled the show on the initial ground due to low occupancy that was not believable,” the bench said.
The commission also noted that the theatre later gave a different reason for the cancellation. It said the theatre had relied on its written version and evidence affidavit but had not produced substantial documentary proof of the alleged technical problem.
“It is also not in dispute that, later the theatre management changed their version stating that ‘the cancellation was due to Technical issue’ that was under suspicious of the truthfulness and Bonafide’s of the Opposite Parties. Neither any technical report nor any technical error cropped-up caused by storage limitation in the Screen AUDI 06 was filed in support of the Contentions of Opposite Party,” it added.
The commission further noted that the ticket amount had been refunded after the show was cancelled. However, it said the refund did not remove the deficiency in service arising from the cancellation.
“It is also an admitted fact that the ticket cost was alleged to be refunded to the original payment mode on 27th January, 2025 under Ex. A-1 as the theatre management abruptly cancelled the show wherein it was mentioned that ‘Still haven’t received the refund’,” the commission further added.
The commission held that the cancellation amounted to deficiency in service and unfair trade practice. It partly allowed the complaint and awarded compensation and litigation costs.
What did the commission order?The Hyderabad district consumer commission directed PVR Inox and the theatre to:
- Pay Rs 5,000 as compensation for deficiency in service and unfair trade practice.
- Pay Rs 1,000 towards litigation costs.
- Pay the total Rs 6,000 jointly and severally.
- Make the payment within 45 days from receiving the order.
- The customer's remaining claims were disallowed.

title: Language Lab Turns 10 and Launches ‘Ukraine Connected,’ a Community for Internationals in Ukraine
content:
For a decade, Kyiv’s Language Lab has taught Ukrainian to foreigners, including online, and along the way become an informal support network for its students, helping with everything from everyday problems to calling an ambulance. Now, marking its tenth anniversary, the school is formalizing that role with Ukraine Connected, a curated community with coordinators, meetups and regular events that aims to become the biggest network for internationals in Ukraine.
For founder Ksenia Golubytska, reaching 10 years is about more than longevity.

“First and foremost, it’s about trust – the trust of my team, my clients, my close ones who supported me along the way, and myself,” she said.
She said the milestone also reflects a deeper shift in how people see the Ukrainian language: “More and more people are finding real importance and value in learning Ukrainian, and being part of that is something I cherish deeply.”
The road was not easy.
“We got through COVID, through the full-scale invasion and ongoing war, and everything that came with it – so reaching 10 years feels earned,” Golubytska said.
Finding its identity
Language Lab did not start out as a Ukrainian-language school. In its early years, Golubytska said, the team experimented with “different languages, different approaches, different formats.”
The school found its clear identity around the time of Russia’s full-scale invasion in 2022, when it settled on Ukrainian and on a format that worked for its clients.
‘This Is My Personal Contribution to Ukraine's Victory’
“That gave us solid ground, a real foundation to build on,” she said.
Over the years, the school has had more than 1,500 clients and more than 200 organized events. Its client list includes major international humanitarian and aid organizations, as well as embassies and diplomatic staff, international and Ukrainian companies, and media outlets such as Kyiv Post, with which it has a partnership.
Golubytska said the school plans to widen its reach further. One goal is to serve Ukrainians in the diaspora who want to reconnect with the language, alongside new courses and formats for different kinds of learners.
More than a language school
Over the years, Language Lab’s role for many foreign students has gone well beyond grammar lessons.
“We’ve become something like an entry point for them into Ukraine,” Golubytska said. That has meant “supporting them, answering questions, helping with everyday problems, even things like calling an ambulance when needed.”
The school has also hosted cultural events and social meetups for its students. Ukraine Connected, Golubytska said, is designed to take that to the next level.
“It’s structured as a social initiative, and to us it feels like a natural, logical continuation of everything the school has been doing all along,” she said.
How Ukraine Connected will work
Members will be able to register and join organized chats around different topics. But Golubytska stressed that the chats are a means, not the goal.
“The main focus isn’t the chat itself – it’s real connection: people meeting in real life or online and doing things together,” she said.
Coordinators will curate who joins and help organize the community’s activities. Members will share recommendations, help each other with urgent questions, and suggest ideas for small meetups and activities. The whole community will gather for larger events at least once every six months.
The initiative is aimed at people who live or work in Ukraine, want to understand Ukrainian culture better, are looking for Ukrainian business partners, are interested in investment opportunities, or want to support and promote Ukraine abroad. Its stated mission is to help foreigners lead a comfortable and fulfilling life in the country.
The ambition is large.
“Our ambition is to build the biggest community for internationals in Ukraine,” Golubytska said.
A bet on Ukraine’s future
For Golubytska, the anniversary is ultimately about looking ahead.
“It’s about hope – hope that this will keep developing, that more people will visit, invest, and move to Ukraine, and that Ukraine will be in the spotlight in the way it deserves,” she said.
“More than anything,” she added, “we want Ukraine Connected to be an entry point – a place that helps people feel at home in Ukraine, genuinely welcomed and part of something, not just passing through.”

title: First Estonian to qualify for LA Paralympics eyes career-best form
content:
First Estonian to qualify for LA Paralympics eyes career-best form
Estonian paralympian swimmer Matz Topkin is the first athlete from his country to so far qualify for the Los Angeles Paralympics, after winning silver in Turkey.
Topkin took silver in the 50m backstroke at the 2026 World Para Swimming European Championships in Kocaeli, Turkey earlier this month. He said the feat gives him room to experiment before the Los Angeles games in 2028.
Topkin's time of 44.95 seconds at his first start of the season secured his place at the LA Olypmics, roughly a week after his medal-winning swim in Turkey.
As to which achievement meant more — the European medal or the Paralympic berth — Topkin said both carried equal weight.
"Firstly, the medal was important to me because I've managed to win a medal at the last three European Championships, and I suppose it's a matter of ego — I can't let my level drop," he said. "I'm glad I won the medal, and I'm even happier that it came with such a good time, especially considering how empty my season has been this year. And to have a Paralympic berth in my pocket as the first Estonian — that's a fantastic headline."
Topkin finished seventh in the 50m backstroke in Paris in 2024, and sixth in Tokyo in 2021. He says he is hoping to improve on those results in 2028.
"The Paralympic Games are always special," he said. "I'm really looking forward to them, because, as you know, the Tokyo and Paris Games didn't really go that well for me. I'm hoping that third time's the charm. Maybe the third time will go a little better."
With qualification secured, Topkin said he can now focus on reaching peak form in two years' time, and may experiment with new training methods ahead of that.
"I may be able to experiment to some extent now that I've met the qualifying standard and don't have to worry about that anymore," he said. "Maybe I can try some new training methods. As we know, [Estonian domestic record-holding swimmer] Ralf Tribuntsov trains over very short distances — it's something to think about, whether I might try something like that as well. Time will tell."

title: Selbstständig mit Behinderung – Mit der Rampe ins Bundeshaus: Julian Mosers Einsatz für Inklusion
content:
Der 19-jährige Julian Moser wohnt mit seiner Zerebralparese selbstständig in einer Wohnung in Zürich. Im Alltag braucht er viel Hilfe: «Grundsätzlich brauche ich überall Hilfe, wo ich Sachen nicht machen kann wegen meiner Behinderung», sagt Moser. Die benötigte Unterstützung erhält er durch eine Assistenzperson. Sie hilft ihm, zu kochen, zu essen, zu trinken, einzukaufen und sich zu kleiden.
Die Assistenz ist vor allem abends und nachts bei Moser. Wenn er tagsüber einen Termin ausser Haus wahrnehmen will, muss er Zusatzstunden beantragen.
Teilhabe am sozialen und beruflichen Leben
Finanziert werden seine täglichen acht Assistenzstunden über die Invalidenversicherung (IV). Er wünscht sich aber mehr Unterstützung, um am sozialen und beruflichen Leben teilnehmen zu können.
Moser wollte eine Lehre anfangen, diese ist aber am verlangten Arbeitspensum gescheitert: «Ich habe dem Bund angeboten, eine Lehre auf 60 Prozent zu machen, die IV hat aber Konditionen an die Lehre geknüpft, die ich nicht erfüllen konnte.»
Denn Moser ist bereits Arbeitgeber: Er koordiniert die Arbeitspläne für seine Assistenzpersonen – das kostet ihn viel Energie. Auch die Physiotherapie nimmt zusätzliche Zeit in Anspruch. Die IV wollte ihm nur eine Lehre auf 80 Prozent finanzieren: mit seinen anderen Verpflichtungen eine zu grosse Überforderung.
Moser kämpft aber für seine Ziele und engagiert sich politisch. Gemeinsam mit anderen Menschen mit Behinderungen ist er am Dienstag nach Bern gereist, um im Bundeshaus für die Anliegen der Inklusionsinitiative zu lobbyieren.
Beschwerliche Reise ins Bundeshaus
Die Reise war anstrengend: «Sobald ich weiss, dass ich einen Termin habe, muss ich Assistenz organisieren, muss die SBB anrufen, um mich anzumelden, dass ich komme. Jeder Mensch mit Behinderung muss das machen.»
Bei der Sicherheitskontrolle beim Bundeshaus mussten er und seine Mitstreiterinnen länger warten. In die Wandelhalle zu gelangen, bereitete Moser aber fast keine Schwierigkeiten. Er nahm die Rampe im Haupteingang und fuhr mit dem Lift nach oben, um Parlamentarierinnen und Parlamentariern von seinen Erfahrungen zu erzählen.
Einen Tag nach Mosers Besuch in Bundesbern diskutierte der Nationalrat intensiv über die Inklusionsinitiative und den indirekten Gegenvorschlag des Bundesrates. Der Rat hat noch keine Entscheidung gefällt, die Diskussionen werden am 21. September weitergeführt. Die Initiative hat schlechte Chancen, während der Gegenvorschlag eine Mehrheit finden könnte.
Inklusionsinitative: Stimmen aus der Nationalratsdebatte
Ob sich die Situation für Julian Moser verbessern wird, ist noch offen. Klar ist: Er will sich weiterhin engagieren und strebt ein politisches Amt an. «Sei es Nationalrat, Ständerat oder Stadtrat, ich sehe mich definitiv in der Zukunft dort.» Sein Vorbild: SP-Nationalrat und Behindertenrechtsaktivist Islam Alijaj. Über Mosers Schreibtisch hängen mehrere Bilder der beiden.

title: Citing barefoot Beed woman’s ‘struggle’, Bombay High Court gives mother children’s custody
content:
5 min readNew DelhiUpdated: Sep 7, 2026 03:30 PM IST

To afford her daughter’s education, 47-year-old Ramabai Ranvir ran three kilometres to win a Rs 3,000 cash prize in Maharashtra’s Beed district. Citing her extraordinary sacrifice while hearing a family matter, the Bombay High Court underlined the heavy burdens mothers often carry to secure their children’s future — and granted a woman custody of her two minor children.
Justice Rajesh S Patil said the incident was a “reminder” that a mother’s struggle to raise and educate her children is not always reflected merely in “figures” placed before the court. Behind those figures often lies a continuing “endeavour” to balance limited means against the ever-growing necessities of food, shelter, education and a dignified existence, he added.
“The court cannot remain ignorant of the realities of life which confront a woman who, while striving to secure the future of her children, is simultaneously required to attend to the necessities of her own day-to-day existence,” the September 3 order observed.
Noting that the husband himself, on a stamp paper, had admitted that he has an extramarital affair, the court held that in such circumstances, it could not be said that the children would be in a healthy environment in the father’s custody.
The high court was hearing a revision plea filed by the mother challenging a sessions court’s order that had granted interim custody of the two minor children to their father till the final disposal of the proceedings, while giving her only visitation rights.
Domestic violence complaint
The wife had filed a domestic violence complaint and an interim application seeking custody of her two children. The application was allowed after the judicial magistrate interviewed both children. Aggrieved, the husband challenged the order before the sessions court, which held that the allegation about the husband’s extramarital affair would not affect the interim application for custody of the minor children.
Justice Rajesh S Patil said the incident in Beed is a ‘reminder’ that a mother’s struggle to raise and educate her children is not always reflected merely in figures placed before the court.
The wife then filed this petition before the high court seeking interim custody of her daughter and son, claiming that she has recently joined the service of a company and earns a salary of Rs 13,000 per month.
Story continues below this ad
‘Children can live with grandparents’
The wife, through advocate Avesh Ghadge, claimed that her parents and her two married brothers live together, and both brothers have taken up the responsibility of her welfare, as well as that of her two children, both emotionally and financially.
She further claimed that her brothers’ children were around the same age as her own children and they would be able to enjoy each other’s company while living together with their maternal grandparents and uncles.
The woman alleged that both children were studying in a CBSE school. However, after the couple started living separately, the husband, whom she accused of often being drunk and also of having an extramarital affair, removed them from the school and admitted them to a state board school.
The husband, through his advocate Vijay V Patil, denied the allegations of an extramarital affair and that he was often inebriated. He submitted that both children were happily staying with him and their grandparents, who were taking care of them with love and affection. It was also argued that their present school was only around 100 to 150 metres from his residence.
Story continues below this ad
The man also claimed that his wife did not have an income source to meet the educational and other expenses of the children.
Children tutored, in-laws helpless: HC
The court found that the wife was not seeking custody as a means of obtaining financial support or any monetary advantage from her husband, as she had not claimed maintenance or alimony for herself. It noted that the daughter, being 12 years old and approaching puberty, would require more company of her mother, while the six-year-old son would also require his mother’s company.
After interacting with both children, the court found that they appeared to have been “tutored” by the husband. It also noted that the woman’s brothers had agreed and orally undertaken to take care of her and her children.
“They (wife and her brothers) do not require any kind of alimony or maintenance from respondent number 1 (husband) for their sister or towards her children,” the court noted.
Story continues below this ad
The court also interacted with the man’s parents and found them to be helpless. “As far as a healthy environment for the upbringing of the children is concerned, it is respondent number 1 (husband) who has, on a stamp paper, admitted that he has an extra-marital affair,” it added.
After considering the case, the court held that for the better future of the children and taking into account a better environment for them, the mother should get their custody.
The court directed the husband to hand over both children to the mother on September 9, and allowed the man to meet the children every Sunday till the final disposal of their case.

title: ¿Cómo se asignan las ayudas para reparar apartamentos afectados por los terremotos en La Guaira?
content:
Las autoridades nacionales comenzaron la entrega de ayudas económicas a propietarios de apartamentos y juntas de condominio afectados por los terremotos del 24 de junio en La Guaira. El programa contempla entre 1.500 y 5.000 dólares para reparaciones independientes dentro de las viviendas y hasta 20.000 dólares para trabajos en áreas comunes gestionados por las juntas de condominio.
En la primera fase en La Guaira fueron incluidos 1.647 propietarios vinculados a 57 juntas de condominio y 70 edificaciones. Estos inmuebles fueron clasificados con etiqueta amarilla por la Comisión Presidencial para la Evaluación de Habitabilidad de Infraestructuras.
Pero recibir la ayuda no significa que todos los propietarios obtengan 5.000 dólares. De hecho, en la primera entrega reportada en La Guaira se transfirieron 2.821,30 dólares a cada una de las 1.647 familias beneficiadas, mientras que medios locales señalaron que en Residencias Parque Mar algunos propietarios recibieron cantidades de entre 1.500 y 3.000 dólares, de acuerdo con reportes de La Verdad de Vargas.
¿Quién puede recibir la ayuda para reparar su apartamento?
El primer paso es que la vivienda aparezca en los registros realizados después de los sismos y que haya sido incluida en las evaluaciones de habitabilidad.
En el caso de la primera fase de La Guaira, los beneficiarios pertenecen a edificaciones que fueron evaluadas y clasificadas con etiqueta amarilla, dentro del proceso de revisión realizado por la Comisión Presidencial para la Evaluación de Habitabilidad de Infraestructuras.
Esto permite distinguir la ayuda de un pago general para todas las personas afectadas por los terremotos. La inscripción en el censo y la evaluación del inmueble forman parte del proceso para determinar quiénes pueden acceder al programa.
La gobernación ha informado que las juntas de condominio son parte importante de este proceso porque reúnen la información de los propietarios y la remiten a las autoridades. Por ello, una persona que no haya sido incluida en el primer listado puede necesitar verificar con su junta si sus datos fueron registrados y cuál es el procedimiento para incorporar su caso.
¿En qué se diferencian las ayudas para los apartamentos y los condominios?
Los recursos individuales están destinados a reparaciones dentro de cada vivienda. Por separado, el programa contempla financiamientos de hasta 20 mil dólares para las juntas de condominio registradas, destinados a intervenir las áreas comunes de los edificios.
Esto quiere decir que una misma residencia puede acceder a dos vías distintas de financiamiento. Un propietario puede recibir un subsidio para reparar su apartamento, mientras la junta puede gestionar recursos para trabajos en espacios compartidos.
Las áreas comunes pueden requerir intervenciones diferentes a las de cada vivienda, por lo que el financiamiento de la junta no se reparte entre los propietarios como si fuera un segundo bono individual.
¿Qué deben hacer quienes todavía no aparecen entre los beneficiarios?
Los propietarios que no fueron incluidos en la primera fase deben verificar con su junta de condominio si fueron incorporados al censo y si el inmueble fue sometido a la evaluación correspondiente.
La información recopilada por las juntas sirve para elaborar los listados que posteriormente son enviados a las autoridades. Por ello, no aparecer en la primera entrega no necesariamente significa que el proceso terminó para ese propietario.
Las autoridades han informado que el programa continuará con nuevas intervenciones y entregas. En La Guaira, además de las reparaciones individuales, se anunció la atención de más edificaciones y familias afectadas por los terremotos del 24 de junio.

title: Air Peace offers 25% discount as compensation for delayed Lagos-Enugu flight
content:
Air Peace airline has offered a lawyer and human rights activist, Inibehe Effiong, a 25 per cent discount on a one-way ticket across its domestic routes as compensation for a delayed Lagos-Enugu flight, in compliance with a directive by the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority.
Effiong disclosed this in a post on his X page on Wednesday, sharing a copy of an email he received from the airline’s call centre.
In the email sighted by our correspondent, Air Peace apologised for the disruption of flight P47100 from Lagos to Enugu on September 21, 2026, and said it had approved a discounted ticket, excluding tax, as compensation for the inconvenience.
“To claim the ticket, please send an email to [email protected] with your old booking reference, scanned copy of your travel passport, and details of your new flight itinerary (route, date and time),” the airline stated.
It added that the offer was valid for six months from the date of the email, excluding the period between December 15, 2026 and January 15, 2027.
PUNCHONLINE had earlier reported that the NCAA directed Air Peace to compensate Effiong and other affected passengers after its preliminary investigation found that the airline sent them a wrong notification ahead of the flight, which was scheduled to depart Lagos for Enugu at 6:45am on Monday.
Effiong had accused the airline of irresponsibility, saying he arrived at Terminal One of the Murtala Muhammed Airport at about 5:50am for the flight, only to be told, along with other passengers, to wait, before it was eventually delayed till 4:50pm.
He said the disruption caused him to miss a scheduled court appearance in Enugu State.
The NCAA’s Director, Public Affairs and Consumer Protection, Michael Achimugu, had subsequently confirmed that the delay was a ripple effect of an earlier disruption on Sunday night, and directed the airline to compensate affected passengers in line with Part 19 of the NCAA Regulations 2023.
Reacting to the compensation offer, Effiong said the gesture did not address what he described as the airline’s recurring poor service culture.
“This modest effort by Air Peace to assuage me and other aggrieved passengers should not detract from the fundamental issue, namely: the perennial lackluster, arrogant and frustrating attitude of the company,” he said, in a post on X
Effiong commended the swift response of Achimugu and the NCAA, but insisted that a stronger regulatory framework was required to protect air passengers’ rights.
“While the swift response of Mike Achimugu and NCAA in this case are commendable, there is no doubt that we need a stiffer and stronger regulatory framework in the aviation industry to protect the rights of air passengers,” he said.

title: I sit with people while they complete their to-do lists. It's been a surprising way to turn patience into a side hustle.
content:
I never thought of myself as particularly patient. Then, my hairdresser mentioned that she'd had the same giant basket of unfolded laundry sitting in her living room for six months.
I offered to come over and help — not by doing her laundry, but by being her "body double." "Body doubling" involves doing a task in the presence of another person to make it easier to stay focused, motivated, and on track.
For some people (particularly those with ADHD), simply having another person nearby can help them finally complete tasks that have been sitting on the to-do list for days — or years.
I'm a textbook Virgo and thrive on organization. I love a color-coded calendar, have a meticulously stocked desk drawer full of cute office supplies, and genuinely find cleaning and organizing my home soothing. However, I'm also a procrastinator extraordinaire. I work best when a deadline is on fire.
Although I haven't been formally diagnosed with ADHD, I've found "body doubling" — whether sitting across from a friend in a coffee shop with our laptops or coworking over Zoom — to be the secret to helping me get work done with as little panic as possible.
I thought that if "body doubling" could help me meet my writing deadlines, perhaps it could help my hairdresser tackle some of her most overwhelming tasks.
This arrangement has helped us both — and I've made a friend in the process
So, my hairdresser and I struck up a deal: I'd come over and sit with her while she tackles the things she's been avoiding (folding laundry, opening mail, hanging up clothes, and other small administrative tasks that somehow become increasingly overwhelming the longer they sit undone).
In exchange, she gives me a discount on my haircuts and complimentary professional color services, including highlights and treatments I never could have justified splurging on before.
In addition to the tasks mentioned above, I've supported my hairdresser in filling out forms to apply for government grants (she's a single mom of three), organizing her email inbox, and even responding unemotionally to tricky messages she's been avoiding.
Mostly though, I sit and keep her company, offering a mix of emotional support, accountability, and occasional enthusiastic sock-pairing.
We've been working together this way since February 2022, and although it's an unusual arrangement for some people, it works for us.
Before I started getting my dark, wavy hair professionally coloured, I'd relied on box dye for the past 20 years. My pitch-black hair was also brittle and thinning.
Since I started getting it professionally colored, it's the healthiest it's been in decades. My hairdresser also managed to bring it back to the dark golden-brown color of my childhood, which feels a bit like getting a piece of myself back.
I've discovered I'm more patient than I thought, and I hope to take on more clients
Watching someone open months' worth of mail isn't how I imagined I'd spend my free time, yet I've discovered I'm surprisingly good at it.
Doing this has also reframed how I think about patience. I have an anxiety disorder, so my mind always feels very busy — hence the reason I've never considered myself to be especially patient. Yet recently, my hairdresser described me as a "calm and steady presence."
I'm honored that someone trusts me enough to show me the messiest, most vulnerable parts of their life, and it's helped me reframe how I see myself and what I have to offer.
When necessary, I can be a firm but kind leader who can slow down and meet people where they're at.
In the past, I would have taken over and just done the tasks myself. Now I understand that sometimes the most helpful thing you can do is make someone feel a little less alone as they start the thing they've been unable to begin.
Either way, I still get to enjoy feeling a sense of accomplishment.
I like "body doubling," and am considering turning it into a more traditional side hustle by taking on paying clients while I search for a new full-time job. I'm still figuring out what that might look like and how much I'd charge, but I'd be lying if I said the prospect of helping more people didn't excite me.
In the meantime, I'm grateful to have access to incredible beauty services — and my hair has never looked better.

title: Hohe Heilungschancen - „Gibt Kinder, die kommen mit Krebs auf die Welt“
content: In der aktuellen Ausgabe von „Wiener Wissen“ analysieren die Direktorinnen des St. Anna Kinderspitals, Caroline Hutter und Sabine Taschner-Mandl, den Status Quo im Bereich Kinderkrebsforschung. Taschner-Mandl: „Die Diagnostik zeigt, welche Gene betroffen sind. Eine Krebserkrankung bei Babys und Kleinkindern betrifft sogar teils auch Zellen, die nur in Embryos vorkommen.“ Hutter: „Es gibt Kinder, die kommen auf die Welt und haben schon Krebs. Natürlich ist Krebs bei Kindern eine Katastrophe. Aber es gibt in Österreich im internationalen Vergleich trotzdem gute Heilungschancen.“ Derzeit würden aufgrund der Fortschritte bei Forschung und Wissenschaft in Österreich schon rund achtzig Prozent krebsbetroffener Kinder ihre Krebserkrankung überleben. Vor dreißig Jahren seien das nur zwanzig Prozent gewesen. Ob diese Heilung dann aber auch dauerhaft sei? Hutter: „Manche Tumorzellen verstecken sich richtig. Die sieht man dann auch in der Nachbehandlung nicht.“ Es gäbe aber auch leichter erkennbare Krebsformen. Taschner-Mandl: „Ein ausgebrochener Tumor ist wie eine ungeformte Masse.“ Hutter: „Der kann auch mehrere Kilo haben. Das ist dann wie ein Knödel. Etwa im Beckenbereich kann man ihn dann auch so richtig erfühlen.“

title: Men incarcerated in Kansas heard families owed $6,000 for lunch, raised funds to help
content:
A group of men incarcerated in Kansas saw a problem in their community and stepped in with money from their own pockets to help solve it.
After learning that Norton Community Schools had accumulated roughly $6,000 in unpaid meal costs, they organized a fundraiser that erased most of the debt.
Here's what to know
On Aug. 3, nearly 30 men incarcerated at Norton Correctional Facility gathered to present Superintendent Corey Roy with a check for $4,267 to put toward the district's unpaid meal accounts.
As local news outlet KWCH reported, an effort to raise the funds was organized through Reaching Out from Within, an organization that has been operating in prisons across Kansas, North Carolina, and Missouri for over four decades to enable member-led healing and rehabilitation.
In the recent Norton fundraiser, individuals participating in the program donated $3,810, and staff from the Kansas Department of Corrections contributed another $457, according to KWCH. With that gift, the district was able to clear the majority of its meal debt, which built up as the school provided breakfasts and lunches to students experiencing food insecurity at home.
More background
A statement shared by the correctional facility noted that many of the men who had donated said they had gone hungry when they were young and believed it had hurt their performance in school. They hoped their efforts would help to ensure that food insecurity would not be a barrier for students as they began the new academic year.
"I was moved at how the men I spoke with wanted to make a positive impact to help others in the community," Roy also said in the statement.
As economic pressures, compounded by energy shocks and hits to agricultural production, contribute to rising food costs across the country, more families are experiencing the strain at home.
At the same time, more than 1.5 million children — and around 5 million people overall — are estimated to have lost access to support through the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, or SNAP, since the One Big Beautiful Bill Act became law in 2025. The estimates were published by the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities last month.
Families could feel even more pressure related to the loss of federal benefits by the end of September, when many SNAP program costs are set to shift to states.
No nationwide solution for school meal debt has yet passed Congress. Many districts still rely on local responses such as donations, nonprofit partnerships, and direct aid for families.
