title: À Utrecht, un quartier sans voitures sort de terre
content:
Pas de voitures garées le long des trottoirs, pas de rues transformées en files de stationnement, et 21 500 emplacements pour vélos. À Utrecht, au centre des Pays-Bas, le futur quartier Merwede entend pousser très loin une idée encore assez radicale ailleurs en Europe : construire un morceau de ville dense en considérant dès le départ que la voiture particulière n’en sera pas le moyen de transport principal. Un projet dans la continuité d’une ville déjà très engagée en faveur du vélo. Utrecht a été classée en 2022 n°1 mondiale du Global Bicycle Cities Index, devant Münster et Anvers. Selon les chiffres municipaux, 94 % des habitants possédaient au moins un vélo en 2021. La ville abrite même, près de la gare centrale, le plus grand parking à vélos du monde, avec 12 500 places.
Merwede n’est plus seulement une vue d’architecte. Sur cet ancien secteur d’activités, coincé entre le canal de la Merwede et le parc Transwijk, les grues ont pris possession du paysage. Sur les 6 000 logements programmés, plus de 2 700 étaient déjà en construction fin 2025. Le 8 juillet 2026, le lancement d’Urban8, un ensemble de 171 logements, a marqué une nouvelle étape.
La voiture reste à la porte
"Sans voitures" ne signifie pas pour autant que leurs propriétaires seront interdits de séjour. Les habitants de Merwede pourront posséder une automobile mais celle-ci ne dormira pas devant leur immeuble ou dans son sous-sol. Le principe de ce nouvel éco-quartier consiste à concentrer le stationnement dans des garages situés à la périphérie du quartier, notamment du côté de l’Europalaan, ou à proposer des possibilités de stationnement encore plus éloignées. À l’intérieur, la priorité revient aux piétons et aux cyclistes.
En outre, pour que l’équation fonctionne, Utrecht ne s’est pas contentée de supprimer des places de parking. Le projet prévoit 250 voitures partagées, de nombreux vélos en libre-service, 21 500 places pour garer les bicyclettes dans les bâtiments et deux centres logistiques pour, notamment, réceptionner les colis. Enfin, les transports publics doivent compléter le dispositif. L’idée est simple : faire de la voiture une option parmi d’autres, et non le moyen de transport autour duquel toute la ville est organisée.
Un concept qui prend peu à peu vie
Une étape assez révélatrice a été franchie le 8 juillet 2026, avec le lancement officiel du chantier d’Urban8, un ensemble de 171 logements. Le bâtiment accueillera un centre de mobilité destiné à plusieurs îlots du nord de Merwede. Il comprendra des services d’autopartage, des équipements pour la réception des colis, un garage mais surtout… 1 332 emplacements pour vélos.
Quelques semaines plus tard, fin août, Utrecht engageait une autre transformation très concrète. Une portion de voie parallèle à l’Europalaan, une grande avenue d’Utrecht jusqu’ici ouverte aux voitures, vélos et piétons, doit être retirée de la circulation automobile pour devenir un axe réservé aux mobilités actives. Les rares accès nécessaires aux automobiles se feront directement depuis l’Europalaan vers les entrées du quartier et ses parkings périphériques. Autrement dit, la municipalité commence à modifier le réseau routier lui-même pour empêcher la voiture de reprendre naturellement sa place.
Que faire des courses, des colis et des déménagements ?
Le plus difficile dans un quartier sans voitures n’est peut-être pas de dessiner de jolies promenades arborées. C’est d’organiser toutes les situations dans lesquelles une automobile ou un utilitaire reste bien pratique : rentrer avec des meubles, recevoir un colis volumineux, accueillir un visiteur, se déplacer lorsque l’on est handicapé ou simplement partir en week-end.
Merwede teste pour cela une gouvernance assez inhabituelle. Un Mobiliteitsbedrijf, une entreprise dédiée à la mobilité du quartier, a notamment été créée pour gérer les abonnements aux parkings, le stationnement des vélos des visiteurs, la sélection des services d’autopartage et de mobilité partagée, mais aussi des boutiques de services et des consignes à colis. Les personnes disposant d’une autorisation de stationnement pour handicapés pourront de leur côté utiliser des emplacements spécifiques dans les parkings.
Vivre sans voiture suppose d’avoir tout à proximité
Le quartier doit parallèlement limiter la nécessité d’aller chercher ailleurs ce qui manque sur place. Aux logements doivent s’ajouter écoles, commerces, restaurants, espaces de travail, équipements sportifs et services de santé. Un bâtiment réunissant un établissement scolaire de 1 000 élèves, une salle de sport et un grand parking public pour vélos doit notamment entrer en chantier en septembre 2027.
Merwede doit également être relié aux quartiers voisins par deux nouvelles passerelles destinées aux cyclistes et aux piétons au-dessus du canal, sans gêner la navigation fluviale. Un point crucial car un quartier sans voitures ne peut fonctionner comme une île. Il doit être plus facile d’en sortir à pied, à vélo ou en transport collectif qu’en automobile. Faute de quoi, la voiture ne disparaît pas : elle se contente de se déplacer quelques centaines de mètres plus loin, avec le risque de reporter stationnement et circulation sur les quartiers voisins.
Le vrai test commencera en 2027
Beaucoup de villes européennes réduisent la place de la voiture dans des quartiers existants mais Utrecht tente ici autre chose : concevoir dès l’origine un quartier dense dans lequel rues, bâtiments, stationnement, livraison des colis et services de mobilité ont été pensés autour de son absence.
Le pari sera réellement confronté au quotidien à partir de 2027, lorsque les premiers habitants emménageront. Il faudra alors voir si les voitures partagées sont disponibles lorsqu’on en a besoin, si les milliers de vélos trouvent effectivement leur place, si les livraisons fonctionnent, si les visiteurs acceptent de marcher quelques centaines de mètres et si les habitants conservent malgré tout une automobile garée ailleurs. Bref, vérifier si l’on peut réellement retirer la voiture de la rue sans compliquer la vie de ceux qui y habitent. Merwede ne sera alors plus seulement un laboratoire d’urbanisme. Il deviendra une expérience grandeur nature.

title: Håkon (17) var sikker på at han hadde ADHD. Hjelpen forandret alt.
content:
Håkon (18) var sikker på at han hadde ADHD.
Men hjelpen han fikk, forandret alt.
Slik hjelp får ikke alle barn.
ADHD-lotteriet
ADHD-lotteriet
NRK har kartlagt bruken av ADHD-medisin blant barn i Norge.
Vi oppdaget at den varierer kraftig, etter hvor barna bor.
I noen kommuner bruker nesten ti ganger så mange barn ADHD-medisin som i andre.
Andelen barn som bruker ADHD-medisin etter kommune.
Forskjellene er enorme fra kommune til kommune.
I kommunen med høyest bruk får hvert tiende barn ADHD-medisin.
I kommunen med lavest bruk får hvert hundrede barn ADHD-medisin.
Kommuner med færre enn ti barn på ADHD-medisin er utelatt av hensyn til personvernet. Kilde: FHI
Nederst i saken kan du se tallene for flere kommuner.
Hvorfor er forskjellene så store?
Vi dro til kommunen med lavest medisinbruk.
Gutten som trodde han hadde ADHD
I Lørenskog møter vi Håkon.
Her bruker bare rundt én prosent av barna ADHD-medisin.
Håkon er 18 år og jobber som tømrerlærling på en byggeplass.
– Jeg synes det er veldig gøy. Det er mye bedre enn motparten, altså skole og sånt, sier han.
For noen år siden slet han med uro og konsentrasjonsvansker. Han følte seg annerledes enn de andre og slet med å passe inn.
– På skolen var jeg ofte ukonsentrert. Jeg var urolig. Klarte ikke følge med på det læreren sa, forteller Håkon.
Etter hvert ble han sikker i sin sak.
– Jeg var overbevist om at jeg hadde ADHD, forteller han.
Også moren hans tenkte det samme.
– Vi ønsket et svar på hvorfor hverdagen var så vanskelig, sier mamma Nancy Gogstad.
Men hun ringte ikke først til BUP, barne- og ungdomspsykiatrien, som utreder ADHD.
Hun ringte til kommunen.
Der fikk hun tak i Renate Horgheim Bjercke.
Vendepunktet
Bjercke er psykologspesialist i Lørenskog kommune og jobber i et lavterskel tilbud for psykisk helse for barn.
Her kan familier ta kontakt, uten å gå via fastlegen.
Hjelpen er gratis.
Bjercke hadde samtaler med Håkon. Hun veiledet foreldrene og ga råd til lærerne hans på skolen.
– Det at vi kunne ringe direkte til en psykolog og få hjelp med en gang, det var kjempeviktig, sier mamma Nancy Gogstad.
Hun mener lavterskeltilbudet ble avgjørende for sønnen.
Han kom seg over kneika. Han hadde ingen ADHD-diagnose. Han trengte ikke medisiner.
– Renate hjalp meg utrolig mye. Jeg fikk et sted å tømme meg for vonde tanker. Jeg slapp å gå bære på det, sier Håkon.
I Lørenskog sier fagfolk at tidlig hjelp kan bidra til at færre barn henvises til ADHD-utredning.
– Barn kan streve med uro av andre grunner enn ADHD. Det kan vi nøste i tidlig, så barnet får riktig hjelp, sier Renate Horgheim Bjercke.
Men slik hjelp finnes ikke overalt.
Mer medisin i distriktene
Når vi ser nærmere på tallene, oppdager vi et geografisk mønster:
Jo mindre sentral kommunen er, jo flere barn får ADHD-medisin.
I mindre sentrale kommuner er andelen dobbelt så høy som i sentrale kommuner.
Hvert tolvte barn på medisin
400 kilometer unna Lørenskog ligger Røros, en landlig kommune sør i Trøndelag.
Den ligger høyt på NRKs liste over medisinbruk.
Her går rundt 8 prosent av barna på ADHD-medisin, altså hvert tolvte barn.
Det er nesten tre ganger høyere enn landsgjennomsnittet.
– Lite hjelp
– 8 prosent! Det er sjokkerende! utbryter Linda Cathrine Herud.
Tre foreldre sitter samlet i en sofa i velhuset på Røros.
Alle har barn som har fått ADHD-diagnose.
De er ikke mot medisiner, men mener barna deres har fått for lite annen hjelp.
– Jeg følte at vi fikk veldig lite hjelp på skolen. Og da mener jeg veldig lite hjelp, sier Kjell Morten Hansen.
– Jeg føler det eneste vi har fått hjelp til, er rett og slett medisineringen. Alle andre tiltak har vi måtte finne ut av selv, sier Monika Goodwine.
Linda Cathrine Herud er enig.
– Det finnes ikke god nok tilrettelegging for alle som sliter på skolen, sier hun.
Hun understreker at noen barn helt klart trenger medisiner.
– Men jeg tror også at det noen ganger er enkleste veien ut, sier Linda Cathrine Herud.
Kortere vei til tablett?
– Nei, det var overraskende tall, sier Vegar Dahl om NRKs kartlegging.
Han er leder av barne- og ungdomspsykiatrisk poliklinikk, BUP, på Røros.
Det er hit barn kommer for utredning, diagnose og behandling.
De siste årene har antall henvisninger for ADHD eksplodert her, forteller Dahl.
– Vi vet at 50 prosent av barna i BUP har en ADHD-diagnose, sier han.
Den høye medisinbruken bekymrer.
Han har en forklaring.
– I flere år har det vært et mangelfullt lavterskeltilbud for barn og unges psykiske helse i Røros, sier han.
Røros er en fattig kommune, og det er få ressurser til ekstra tiltak for barn som sliter, ifølge Dahl.
– Da øker presset på å medisinere, både fra foreldre og skole som ønsker at barnet skal få hjelp, forklarer han.
– Betyr det at det er lettere å gi tablett enn tiltak?
– Terskelen for å gi medisin vil være lavere, hvis man ikke har andre tiltak, svarer Dahl.
– Er det tilfelle her?
– Det kan se sånn ut, sier han.
Dahl understreker at medisiner kan ha god effekt for mange.
Men fagmiljøet er bekymret for den høye bruken.
– Jeg tror at hvis vi hadde hatt bedre tiltak i førstelinjetjenesten, så hadde vi medisinert mindre, sier Dahl.
Han mener hjelpen barna får, henger sammen med hvor de bor.
– Det er store ressursforskjeller mellom kommuner i Norge. Det fører til at barn får ulikt tilbud og ulik oppfølging.
Tidlig hjelp – færre diagnoser
En fersk rapport utarbeidet på oppdrag fra Helsedirektoratet peker i samme retning.
Den har sett på hjelpen barn får i kommunene, og hvor mange som får ADHD.
Mønsteret er tydelig: Kommuner som bruker mer på veiledning og forebygging, har færre barn med ADHD.
Folkehelseinstituttet (FHI) ser det samme.
– Små kommuner med få ressurser til forebygging har ofte flere diagnoser og mer bruk av medisiner, sier Heidi Aase. Hun er avdelingsdirektør i FHI.
Hun påpeker at andre trekk, som befolkningssammensetning, også kan bidra til forskjellene.
– Unger burde ha like muligheter
I sofaen på velhuset blir foreldrene opprørte over forskjellene.
To av dem har barn som har blitt ung ufør.
De mener tidligere hjelp kunne gjort en forskjell for barna.
– Jeg tror det hadde vært som dag og natt, sier Linda Cathrine Herud
– Det burde jo ikke være sånn. Ungene våre burde ha like muligheter som alle andre, sier hun.
– Ikke alltid vi lykkes
Ingvild Prøsch-Moen er kommunalsjef for oppvekst i Røros. Hun sier det er trist å høre at foreldre mener de ikke får hjelpen de trenger.
– Det er ikke bestandig vi lykkes. Det erkjenner vi, sier Prøsch-Moen.
Hun avviser samtidig at det ikke har vært tiltak rundt barn som strever.
Men Røros har hittil ikke hatt et lavterskeltilbud for barn og unge, som det de har i Lørenskog.
– Men det er i oppstartsfasen nå. Der kan barn og foreldre selv ta kontakt, forteller Prøsch-Moen.
– Takknemlig
Tilbake i Lørenskog borer Håkon hull til viftekanal i et nybygg.
18-åringen fra Lørenskog vil fortelle historien sin fordi han vet at det kan gå bra. Han ønsker at andre barn skal få samme mulighet.
– Hvis jeg ikke hadde fått den hjelpa, hadde jeg mest sannsynlig ikke vært i det yrket jeg var i nå. Så jeg er utrolig glad for at jeg er det og fikk den hjelpa, sier Håkon.
Her kan du sjekke din kommune
Hold over kartet for å se hvor mange barn som bruker ADHD-medisin.
Kommuner der færre enn ti jenter eller gutter bruker medisin, er anonymisert.
Landsgjennomsnittet er på 2,68 prosent.
Forskjellene er store
Se hvem som er på topp og bunn.
Hei!
Har du tanker om denne saken du vil dele med meg? Eller tips til nye saker? Da setter jeg stor pris på om du sender meg en e-post.

title: Lọc máu cho người suy thận kèm HIV
content:
Lọc máu cho người suy thận kèm HIV
TP HCMÔng Kiên, 50 tuổi, suy thận cấp trên nền bệnh thận mạn và HIV, được lọc máu cấp cứu và điều trị các bệnh nền giúp hồi phục sau ba tháng.
Ông Kiên đến Trung tâm Tiết niệu - Thận học - Nam khoa, Bệnh viện Đa khoa Tâm Anh TP HCM tái khám hồi giữa tháng 9. Xét nghiệm cho thấy độ lọc cầu thận đạt 59 ml/phút/1,73m², về mức bệnh thận mạn giai đoạn 3A, bệnh nhân không còn phải lọc máu. BS.CKI Mạch Thị Chúc Linh, khoa Nội thận - Lọc máu, cho biết ông Kiên trong nhóm bệnh nhân đặc biệt được điều trị tổn thương thận cấp trên nền bệnh thận mạn kèm bệnh nền HIV, tăng huyết áp, đái tháo đường và viêm gan C.
10 năm nay, ông Kiên điều trị ổn định bệnh thận mạn giai đoạn 3A và uống thuốc điều trị theo phác đồ ARV để ức chế virus HIV. Giữa tháng 7/2024, ông đột ngột ngất xỉu, cấp cứu ở bệnh viện địa phương xét nghiệm ghi nhận chức năng thận suy giảm, ure tăng gấp 3 lần bình thường, creatinine tăng vọt gấp gần 10 lần. Ông được đặt catheter (ống thông nhỏ) tĩnh mạch đùi lọc máu cấp cứu, thoát nguy kịch nhưng cần tiếp tục lọc máu và theo dõi lâu dài, được khoa Nội thận - Lọc máu, Bệnh viện Đa khoa Tâm Anh tiếp nhận.
Bác sĩ Linh cho biết người nhiễm HIV khi mắc bệnh thận phải được kiểm soát nhiễm khuẩn chặt chẽ. Quá trình lọc máu không chỉ nhằm thay thế tạm thời chức năng thận mà cần đồng thời kiểm soát nhiễm trùng, rà soát thuốc, duy trì điều trị ARV và theo dõi các bệnh nền.
Theo bác sĩ Linh, bệnh nhân HIV vốn đã suy giảm sức đề kháng, việc lọc máu nhiều lần mỗi tuần đòi hỏi phải chọc kim vào mạch máu hoặc duy trì catheter. Chỉ cần nhiễm trùng tại vị trí đường vào mạch máu cũng có thể tiến triển thành nhiễm khuẩn huyết, nặng hơn là sốc nhiễm trùng. Đặc biệt, catheter lọc máu có nguy cơ nhiễm khuẩn cao hơn nhiều so với cầu nối động-tĩnh mạch (AVF).
Bác sĩ đánh giá ông Kiên vẫn duy trì lượng nước tiểu tốt, không bị ứ dịch và cân nặng gần như ổn định nên vẫn còn khả năng hồi phục chức năng thận. Êkíp vừa lọc máu hỗ trợ vừa theo dõi khả năng hồi phục của thận.
Ông được lọc máu cấp cứu không siêu lọc 2 lần/tuần để loại bỏ các chất độc, không rút dịch, đồng thời theo dõi lượng nước tiểu, cân nặng, huyết áp, điện giải và diễn tiến chức năng thận. Theo bác sĩ Linh, việc không rút nước giúp duy trì thể tích tuần hoàn và tưới máu thận, tạo điều kiện cho phần mô thận còn khả năng hồi phục chức năng.
Người bệnh nhiễm HIV nên biến chứng phức tạp hơn, các chất độc hại tích tụ, đối mặt với phù phổi, suy tim, tăng kali máu và hội chứng ure huyết cao. Bác sĩ điều chỉnh thuốc kháng virus theo độ lọc cầu thận, tránh làm tăng nặng các bệnh nền liên quan. Ông Kiên được bố trí lọc máu tại phòng riêng, sử dụng máy lọc chuyên biệt đi kèm hệ thống dây quả lọc sử dụng một lần và tiêu hủy theo quy trình.
Chức năng thận của ông Kiên dần hồi phục, từ trên 30 ml/phút/1,73m² về gần mức nền, creatinine giảm xuống 6 lần so với thời điểm cấp cứu, còn hơn 200 µmol/L. Sau 3 tháng, ông Kiên được ngừng lọc máu cấp cứu, chuyển sang theo dõi ngoại trú, tái khám định kỳ và uống thuốc theo chỉ định để duy trì chức năng thận ổn định.
Bác sĩ Linh cho biết trước đây người bệnh HIV bị suy thận gặp khó khăn để tìm nơi lọc máu định kỳ, do nhiều cơ sở y tế thiếu trang thiết bị cách ly chuyên biệt. Hiện, nhiều cơ sở y tế chủ động bố trí hệ thống phòng lọc máu và máy lọc riêng biệt cho bệnh nhân HIV, áp dụng quy trình kiểm soát nhiễm khuẩn nghiêm ngặt giúp người bệnh lọc máu an toàn kết hợp điều trị liệu pháp ART.
Bác sĩ lưu ý người bệnh thận mạn có bệnh nền HIV không tự ý sử dụng các loại nước lá hoặc bài thuốc truyền miệng không rõ nguồn gốc vì nguy cơ chứa các thành phần gây tổn thương thận. Nếu có dấu hiệu mệt nhiều, phù, tiểu ít, buồn nôn, khó thở hoặc các bất thường sau khi sử dụng một loại thuốc, nước lá hay sản phẩm không rõ nguồn gốc, người bệnh cần đến bệnh viện khám sớm để can thiệp kịp thời.
Tổn thương thận cấp nếu phát hiện và xử trí kịp thời có cơ hội hồi phục đáng kể. Tổn thương nặng hoặc kéo dài có thể khiến chức năng thận suy giảm thêm và làm tăng nguy cơ tiến triển bệnh.
Hà Thanh
*Tên người bệnh đã được thay đổi

title: Doctors Diagnosed Her With a Rare Cancer and Gave Her Months to Live. She Survived and Opened a $500,000 Fitness Franchise.
content:
Doctors Diagnosed Her With a Rare Cancer and Gave Her Months to Live. She Survived and Opened a $500,000 Fitness Franchise.
The former PepsiCo executive was drawn to Hotworx, a 24/7 fitness studio franchise offering infrared sauna workouts.
Key Takeaways
- Gwynda Jones turned a major personal health setback and a long corporate career into an entrepreneurial second act, opening a Hotworx franchise in downtown Chicago in 2023.
- Hotworx is a 24/7 fitness studio franchise that combines exercise with infrared saunas.
- Jones funded the venture largely with retirement savings accumulated over 38 years.
As a corporate executive for PepsiCo for 30 years, Gwynda Jones was accustomed to high-intensity work. Then health complications derailed her ambitions.
“In 2013, I had a heart attack and stroke and was disabled,” Jones says in a new interview with Entrepreneur. “Over the years, I did all the therapy. I was determined to get well.”
Around 2019, Jones was no longer disabled, but she knew she couldn’t go back to that executive job. It had required extensive travel, which she could no longer do. She started thinking about other ways to exercise her business acumen while still preserving her health. Her answer was franchising, and her focus was on something simple.
Her research eventually brought her to Hotworx, a 24/7 fitness studio franchise offering infrared sauna workouts. Members choose a 30- or 15-minute workout conducted in infrared sauna rooms.
“I started looking into it,” Jones says. “I didn’t know much about it except that it’s a franchise, you’ll need a staff of four or five, you don’t have to hire instructors because it’s all virtually instructed. Hey, I think I can do that, right?”
Right when she was about to start her business, the Covid-19 pandemic hit. Jones put her franchise plans on pause.
Shortly after came an earth-shattering diagnosis: She had a rare, aggressive form of cancer with no cure. Doctors gave her six months to live and said they were going to give her six treatments of chemotherapy to extend her life long enough to get her affairs in order for her daughter, Monica Nia, who was in college at the time.
Starting chemo
Jones didn’t know where to turn. One of her friends told her about a holistic cancer treatment center in Arizona and encouraged her to call. With nowhere else to go, Jones called the center and asked them what to do.
They told her to clean up her diet, start juicing and cut out white sugar and white flour. They also recommended various therapies, including infrared therapy, which aligned with what Hotworx offered.
Jones thought that Hotworx was closed because of the pandemic, so she followed all of the recommendations besides infrared therapy. She went for her first chemotherapy treatment, “the strongest they had,” and didn’t experience the standard side effects, like nausea and vomiting.
Two weeks after her first chemo treatment, she got a phone call from Hotworx inviting her to a free workout session. When Jones mentioned that everything was shut down due to the pandemic and she couldn’t go, the Hotworx representative said that the city allowed the fitness studio to remain open because it isolated one person per infrared sauna room.
“It was pandemic-proof,” Jones says.
Jones went to her first infrared sauna workout and “felt so good” that she knew she had to do it again. She immediately signed up for a membership, which usually costs between $59 and $99 a month.
“I think part of it was because we were in the pandemic and it was just a place to go,” Jones says. “I can get out of my house and be safe. So I started going.”
A second lease on life
Weeks after her first chemo treatment, Jones went in for her second dose. The doctor told her that something unusual had happened: Her lab work was better than it was before, and it was supposed to be worse. They expected her body to deteriorate, but the lab work showed that it was doing the reverse.
The doctor ordered an emergency scan. When Jones first came to the hospital, she had three large tumors in her liver. Because her cancer was so aggressive, she should have had at least six or more tumors at that point. Instead, the doctor said that of the three original tumors, one was gone and the other two had shrunk. There were no additional tumors.
The doctor told her to continue with what she was doing and keep coming back for additional chemotherapy.
By the time Jones came in for her sixth chemotherapy treatment, she was hopeful. The doctor finally sat her down and told her what she longed to hear: that “not a trace of cancer” was in her body. Subsequent follow-up appointments showed that the cancer remained gone months and years after Jones finished chemotherapy.
With this second lease on life, Jones was ready to start a franchise. She called Hotworx and said, “Give me my license, let’s roll.”
She opened the doors to her studio in downtown Chicago on January 23, 2023.
Funding her own franchise
Jones, 67, did not take out a conventional bank loan to open her Hotworx location. Instead, she drew on the retirement savings she had accumulated during nearly four decades in corporate America.
Before opening a franchise, Jones spent 30 years at PepsiCo and another eight years at GT Data Services. She began contributing to a 401(k) when she was 25 years old after receiving formative advice from a boss: Whenever she got a raise, she should put half of it into her retirement account.
That early lesson shaped her financial life. By age 30, Jones says she had accumulated about $40,000 in her retirement account. She used a 401(k) loan to help cover the down payment on a downtown Chicago condo, then continued saving as her income rose. Later, she says, she used retirement-account loans for other major life expenses, including her wedding and a home purchase.
“Major things, borrow money from yourself,” Jones says. “Because you’re getting raises all along the way too.”
Over time, the account grew substantially. By the end of her career, Jones says her 401(k) balance had reached approximately $1.2 million. She ultimately invested close to $600,000 in the studio.
“Chicago was a lot because it’s expensive,” Jones says. “I did it in the most expensive neighborhood in Chicago. I did it in River North, downtown Chicago.”
The first two years were difficult, she says. The third year was when she really started making money.
Jones says the business generated more than $500,000 in annual revenue last year, though she stressed that figure did not account for expenses. On a monthly basis, she estimates that the studio produces roughly $20,000 to $30,000 in profit during stronger periods.
Why she chose to open a franchise
Jones says she chose a franchise rather than attempting to build an independent fitness business because she wanted the systems, vendors, marketing support and operating playbook that came with an established brand.
“I don’t know what I’m doing,” she says. “Under franchise, you have a marketing team, you have all the systems that they use, and they have all the vendors that you partner with.”
That support includes marketing assistance, payroll vendors, equipment support, IT resources and a network of other franchise owners. Jones says she would have struggled to navigate all of those functions independently during the earliest months of ownership.
“If I was doing this myself, I would have failed the first six months,” she says. “There’s no way.”
Jones says the franchise community itself has become one of the most valuable parts of ownership. She opened when Hotworx had roughly 323 studios; the chain has since grown to about 900 locations, she discloses.
For Jones, that support system also makes the business more transferable than a fitness studio built around a single trainer’s personal brand. Her daughter has joined her as a franchisee co-owner, and the pair are exploring a second location.
“My business can run without me,” Jones says. “Plus, I can easily transfer this over to my daughter if something happened to me.”

title: Por unanimidade, STF iguala tempo de licenças-maternidade e adotante
content:
Publicidade
O Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) decidiu nesta quarta-feira (23) unificar os prazos de licença-maternidade e licença-adotante para mulheres.
Por unanimidade, os ministros julgaram procedente uma ação da Procuradoria-Geral da República (PGR) para igualar o tempo dos benefícios.
Pelo entendimento firmado pela Corte, mães genitoras e adotantes têm direito às licenças remuneradas de 120 dias, que podem ser prorrogadas por mais 60 dias, independentemente do tipo de vínculo trabalhista.
O prazo deve ser contado a partir do parto ou obtenção da guarda. Nos casos de internação da mãe, o prazo vale a partir da alta da mãe ou do bebê, o que ocorrer por último.
Conforme a decisão, a nova regra vale para licenças futuras e para as que estão em andamento.
Entenda
A ação julgada pela Corte foi protocolada pela PGR em outubro de 2023 e pretendeu estender o tempo das licenças-maternidade e adotante previsto na Consolidação das Leis do Trabalho (CLT), regra da iniciativa privada, para as outras categorias, como as servidoras públicas, que são regidas pela Lei 8.112/1990.
Continua depois da publicidade
Pela CLT, as mães biológicas e adotantes têm direito a 120 dias de licença, prazo que pode ser prorrogado por mais 60 dias em empresas que participaram do Programa Empresa Cidadã. Já as servidoras gestantes também podem tirar 120 dias, mas as adotantes só têm direito a 90. No caso do Ministério Público, a licença adotante cai para 30 dias.
Para PGR, o tratamento desigual em relação ao regime de contratação da mulher é inconstitucional.
Julgamento
O julgamento da ação começou na última quarta-feira (16), quando o ministro Alexandre de Moraes, relator do caso, proferiu o seu voto.
Continua depois da publicidade
No entendimento do ministro, as licenças têm objetivo de criar vínculo afetivos entre mães e filhos e não podem possuir prazos diferenciados.
Em seguida, os ministros Flávio Dino, Dias Toffoli e Cármen Lúcia acompanharam o relator.
Na sessão de hoje, os ministros Cristiano Zanin, André Mendonça, Nunes Marques, Luiz Fux e Gilmar Mendes proferiram seus votos, e o julgamento foi encerrado.

title: Six TVET schools benefit from Rwf16bn infrastructure project
content: The Rwanda TVET Board (RTB) has inaugurated new and rehabilitated infrastructure worth €10 million (about Rwf16 billion) at six Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) schools across the country. The facilities were developed under the third phase of the RTB-KfW TVET Project, a partnership between the governments of Rwanda and Germany, with funding provided through Germany’s development bank, KfW. The inauguration ceremony took place at Busasamana Technical Secondary School (TSS) in Nyanza District on September 23. It was attended by the Minister of State for Education, Claudette Irere, and Germany’s Ambassador to Rwanda, Heike Uta Dettmann. The project involved the construction and rehabilitation of student dormitories, dining facilities, classrooms and workshops to improve learning and living conditions for TVET students. The six beneficiary schools are Busasamana TSS in Nyanza District, ES Kinazi TSS in Ruhango District, Father Ramon TSS in Kamonyi District, Karengera TSS in Nyamasheke District, St Augustin Mibirizi TSS in Rusizi District, and ETO Gatumba TSS in Ngororero District. ALSO READ: Govt partners with German institutions to promote TVET Speaking at the ceremony, Irere said the investment goes beyond infrastructure development, describing it as an investment in young people and their ability to contribute to the country's development. She said the partnership has enabled Rwanda to improve infrastructure, provide modern training equipment and strengthen training capacity across key technical secondary schools. However, she emphasised that the new facilities must translate into better training and improved preparation of students for employment and entrepreneurship. “A modern workshop is only valuable when it helps students develop the skills and confidence required to succeed. State-of-the-art tools and equipment only make a difference when learners know how to use them safely, effectively, and creatively,” she said. “Our responsibility is therefore clear. This investment must lead to measurable improvements in the quality of training and, ultimately, in students’ readiness for the labour market and entrepreneurship.” Irere said the government expects graduates to use their acquired skills not only to seek employment but also to develop solutions and establish businesses. “We wish to see young people leave these schools not simply searching for opportunities, but equipped with the tools and capabilities to create solutions, build enterprises, secure decent employment, and contribute meaningfully to their own development as well as that of the country,” she said. ALSO READ: Rwanda secures over $100m to set up TVET centres of excellence The minister urged school managers, instructors and local leaders to ensure the facilities are properly used and maintained to benefit future generations of learners. “Every classroom, workshop, machine, and piece of equipment must be properly used and carefully maintained so that they can serve not only today’s learners but generations of young learners to come,” she said. She also called on instructors to adopt modern teaching practices and ensure training programmes respond to changing industry needs. “Modern equipment must be matched by modern teaching practices, close supervision, and training that responds to the changing needs of various industries,” she said. Addressing students, Irere urged them to make the most of the opportunities provided by the investment. “Make the most of this opportunity, work hard, master your chosen profession, and uphold the highest ethical and professional standards,” she said. Germany pledges continued support for TVET Ambassador Dettmann welcomed the completion of the rehabilitation works, highlighting the importance of improved facilities, including kitchens and bathrooms, to students' daily lives. She said cooperation between Rwanda and Germany in technical and vocational education has a long history and draws on Germany's dual vocational training system, which combines classroom learning with practical workplace training. Dettmann said the completion of the third phase does not mark the end of the partnership. “The rehabilitation is complete, but as we have seen during the signing ceremony, the cooperation is not finished,” she said. “We will continue. We will concentrate on Rwanda because this is how Germany works. In our partnership, we take the lead from Rwanda.” RTB Director General Paul Umukunzi said the board is also implementing the fourth and fifth phases of the project, which have a combined value of €29 million (about Rwf48 billion). He said RTB has also signed a new agreement with KfW for a €16 million (about Rwf26 billion) project aimed at supporting young girls to pursue TVET studies and develop their skills. The completion of the third phase brings the total number of schools supported under the programme to 19, following five schools in the first phase and eight in the second. Busasamana boarding capacity more than doubles Elyse Mwumvaneza, head teacher of Busasamana TSS, said the new facilities have significantly increased the school's capacity to accommodate students. “Before this building was constructed, we used to receive 170 students in boarding, but now the number has increased to 430,” he said. The newly constructed dining hall can accommodate 500 students, while the boys' dormitory has a capacity of 168 students and the girls' dormitory can accommodate 120. Mwumvaneza said the expanded facilities will enable the school to accommodate more learners and provide a better environment for technical and vocational training.

title: TOLIARA - L’axe principal de la ville réhabilité
content: Les gros trous qui parsemaient la chaussée aux abords du stationnement de Sanfily ne sont désormais plus qu’un mauvais souvenir. En période de pluies, de l’eau stagnante atteignant jusqu’aux hanches a fait le calvaire des usagers de la rue et des voyageurs qui prennent les taxi-brousses, qui n’ont pas eu le choix que de se tremper dans l’eau pour rejoindre les véhicules. Sanfily est en effet le principal stationnement de Toliara où les véhicules mini-car de marque Sprinter et Crafter, mais également les camions taxi-brousse ou « karandalana » se côtoient nuit et jour pour desservir l’axe Nord vers la RN9, l’Est-sud vers la RN10 et le Centre-est vers la RN7. C’est ainsi un axe principal par lequel passe la RN7 qui finit un kilomètre plus loin, au jardin de la mer de Toliara. RénovationLes habitants des quartiers d’Andabizy, de Motombe, d’Ankilimarovahatse, de Sanfily et d’Andakoro passent par Sanfily pour rejoindre la ville, pour ramener les élèves ou pour aller aux bureaux. Les cyclo-pousses et les tricycles à moteur, notamment, ont eu du mal à circuler sur cet axe avec les énormes trous en plein milieu de la chaussée, ainsi que les trous en « escalier», faisant parfois renverser des cyclo-pousses.Le ministère des Travaux publics a réhabilité 800 m de cette voie principale, longtemps en restée en mauvais état. « Les travaux de réhabilitation, partant du PK 925+000 jusqu’au PK 925+800, avancent à grands pas. La particularité de cette nouvelle chaussée est qu’elle est refaite en béton », note le ministère. La présence des dallots de déversement sur les côtés est également constatée. L’absence de ces ouvrages permettant l’écoulement de l’eau vers la mer a en effet longtemps fait défaut et contribué à accentuer les inondations dans cette partie de la ville.La réhabilitation est, jusqu’ici, réalisée à moitié. Toutefois, une voie, ayant rempli les conditions qu’il faut pour une chaussée en béton, est actuellement ouverte à la circulation. Elle avait été interdite au passage, même aux piétons, pendant un mois. Les travaux continuent avec le ferraillage, partant du rond-point jusqu’au bureau de la gendarmerie de Sanfily. Soit une partie de la plus belle avenue de Toliara, l’avenue « Monja Jaona ».Mirana Ihariliva

title: Compassionate mind training as school-based social and emotional learning: extension to younger pupils and effects of programme dosage
content: IntroductionThe transition from primary/elementary to high-school education is associated with increased mental health difficulties, especially anxiety. Previously, compassionate mind training (CMT) has been demonstrated to stem anxiety increases and improve prosocial behaviours in children aged 11–12. We extended this research by exploring CMT training effects via two further studies: (i) younger children aged 10–11, and (ii) a shortened/compacted delivery length with children aged 11–12.MethodWe used a mixed methods convergent parallel approach, collecting both quantitative and qualitative data from 110 pupils (m = 56; female = 52; 2 = other) using randomised cluster-controlled designs. In Study 1 (S1), 60 primary pupils aged 10–11 took part in standard Personal, Social, Health and Economic (PSHE) lessons (control n = 30) or CMT lessons (experimental n = 30) over a 6-week period. In Study 2 (S2), 50 secondary pupils aged 11–12 took part in standard PSHE (control n = 25) or CMT (experimental n = 25) lessons over a 4-week period. Data collected included lesson implementation efficacy, standardized measures of anxiety, perfectionism, compassion, stress, wellbeing, and open-ended question data.ResultsS1 Pupils reported positively on their experiences of the CMT lessons, content, and practices. Mixed-factorial ANOVAs demonstrated reductions in trait anxiety and increases in self-compassion and general wellbeing for the CMT group only. For the CMT lessons, thematic analyses further revealed that content and practices positively impacted emotion understanding and literacy, emotion regulation, and prosociality. S2 Implementation efficacy was considerably lower than in the previous research and S1. Mixed-factorial ANOVAs returned no significant interaction effects. Thematic analyses revealed that lesson content and practices positively impacted emotion understanding, regulation, and the classroom climate, but also highlighted challenges of compacted delivery.DiscussionThis research demonstrated repeated efficacy of the CMT lessons with younger children, but reduced self-wellbeing effectiveness with same-age children when the number of delivery sessions was reduced. We argue that this is because social and emotional learning (SEL) requires time to embed, including repeated practice of the introduced knowledge, practices, and skills. Additionally, as a policy response to ongoing PSHE/SEL concerns in the UK, our research demonstrates an example of best practice methodology, balancing power, rigour, and mixed methods designs with ethical and moral requirements to minimise the potential for harm.

title: Poland’s Catholic church recruits priests from Africa and Asia to stave off vocations crisis
content:

By Marcin Choduń (published in cooperation with Tygodnik Powszechny)
With the number of Poles training to be priests falling steadily, Catholic parishes are increasingly looking beyond Europe to fill the gaps.
Father Fransiskus Laka will never forget his first day in Poland. When he stepped out of the arrivals hall at Warsaw’s Okęcie (now Chopin) airport in October 1999, he thought he would not last long. Why? The bitter chill in the air. “It was only seven degrees,” he laughs.
It is not surprising that the young man from Indonesia was having second thoughts. At home, a cool day meant 25°C. Now, though, having spent 27 years in Poland, no weather fazes him. In the middle of winter, he will sometimes even go out in just a T-shirt to shovel snow or bring wood for the stove.
Father Fransiskus has settled in the village of Brzegi, near Zakopane in southern Poland, where he has been parish priest for the last two years. And the mountainous Podhale region it is part of still has long, cold and snowy winters.
Father Fransiskus, a Verbite, is not the only foreign Roman Catholic priest working in Poland, where around 70% of the population is Catholic. Their numbers are growing every year in response to the rising shortage of Polish priests. Polish dioceses are increasingly keen to invite young foreigners to study at their seminaries.
Poland’s shortage of priests
Most of those invited are from Africa. In Kielce, for example, there are currently two seminarians from the Central African Republic and seven from Angola. The Tarnów seminary also trained a priest from the Central African Republic in recent years (ordained as a deacon in the nearby village of Szynwałd in 2024).
In the diocese of Ełk, Bishop Jerzy Mazur announced in a letter read out in churches in 2023 that he would be combating the shortage of priests by inviting clergy from Africa to the diocesan seminary. In return for receiving training in Poland, the newly ordained priests were to spend at least a few years working in the region.
Previously, the support of retired priests had been sufficient. But, as the shortage grew, the curia even considered reducing the number of services or merging parishes. That was when the idea of seeking help from abroad came about.
Just one new priest was ordained in Łódź, Poland's fourth largest city, this year – the lowest figure ever recorded
One church figure admits there has been a “dramatic decline” in interest in the priesthood while the head of a seminary calls it a “crisis” https://t.co/QuwKsoPSg3
— Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 13, 2023
“Priests from Poland increasingly work for as long as their health permits,” says Andrzej Kobyliński, a priest and ethicist from Cardinal Stefan Wyszynski University in Warsaw. “However, that doesn’t change the fact that, in a few years’ time, we’ll have a staffing shortfall, because Polish seminaries are more and more deserted.”
In recent years, a lack of recruits has led to several seminaries merging or closing down. The Wrocław, Legnica and Świdnica seminaries have been combined into one institution – which in reality means the two smaller schools being transferred to the big city.
Clerical students in Kalisz have met a similar fate, having to go to Częstochowa to study, while seminarians from Elbląg have been sent to Olsztyn. The seminaries in Łowicz and Bydgoszcz have closed, and education in Drohiczyn and Sandomierz has been suspended.
“The changes are happening at such an alarming rate that at present over a dozen seminaries will need to be closed,” says Kobyliński. “Let’s take the Płock diocese. You could say that the students in the seminary there are being put through a mental ordeal.”
“Since there are currently 13 seminarians studying in seven year groups, that means that some years are empty or only have one or two people. That causes terrible loneliness. Because how can you survive seven years on your own?”
For Kobyliński, the Ełk diocese is a symbol of the changes that are coming. This year, it only ordained one deacon – from Togo, West Africa.
A new home in Poland
The deacon’s name is Roger and he arrived in Poland a few years ago, along with another prospective priest from Togo who decided to return home for personal reasons.
“There are currently seven people studying in our seminary, three of them from Africa. Apart from Roger, we have two more, from Ghana,” says Marcin Maczan, chancellor of the Ełk curia. According to him, however, the presence of African seminarians in Ełk is not only a response to the shortage of priests.
“Bishop Jerzy Mazur, who himself spent several years working in Ghana and in the past was the head of the missions committee of the Polish Episcopal Conference, is familiar with the realities of mission dioceses. He knows very well that they can always use help in training priests.”
“So these two ideas were combined: training a priest for his home diocese in Africa and his ministry in Poland for eight to ten years after ordination. All in line with the terms of the agreements that the bishop of Ełk made with bishops in Africa,” Maczan says.
These agreements vary. Some priests return to their home dioceses shortly after ordination – seminarians from Kielce, for instance. Others remain for many years, such as Father Fransiskus Laka, whose stay in Poland is prolonged by the congregation’s provincial superior every three years.
Poland was not his first choice. Shortly before being ordained, each of the clerical students in Fransiskus’s seminary, the Divine Word Missionaries in Pieniężno, northeastern Poland, was supposed to name three countries where they wished to serve. He chose Ecuador, Nicaragua and, in last place, Poland.
Usually, one of the first two options is selected, but the provincial superior suggested otherwise. A surprised Fransiskus agreed, and he has never regretted his decision. After spending the first four years in the parish in Pieniężno, he returned to the seminary to become a prefect, responsible for keeping order.
In this period, he travelled the length and breadth of Poland to lead retreats in parishes. He then spent seven years as a curate in Chludów, near Poznań, before in 2024 becoming the priest of the parish of St Anthony in Brzegi in the Podhale region.
“I arrived on 8 December – so almost immediately I had Christmas pastoral visits to make to parishioners’ homes,” says Father Fransiskus.
“They really welcomed me very warmly. They often help me – show me how to light the stove, or leave food outside my door. I learn hard work, humility, patience and faith from them. The mountains are tough terrain – you really need grit to survive.”
Poland became home. Fransiskus feels safe here – despite growing hostility towards foreigners, which is particularly visible in the public and online space (foreign ministry statistics confirm that in 2024-2025 the total number of hate crimes reported in Poland increased by more than 50% – from 760 to almost 1,200 cases).
“I’ve never yet encountered any hostile behaviour towards me,” says Fransiskus.
Although he regularly visits his home island of Lembata, there are many things in Indonesia that he can no longer accept. The organisation of mass, for example: if it is supposed to begin, say, at 7 a.m., worshippers turn up just before 9. They don’t understand why Fransiskus sees this as a problem.
Or a bus journey – when the driver passes his house, he’ll usually take a break to have lunch and play with his children. “The passengers wait patiently and no one thinks anything of it,” laughs Fransiskus.
The Togolese footballing priest
Father Romuald Mawakina Tchilabalo Mozou, from Togo (pictured top), is a newer arrival in Poland. His stay in the country is on the same basis as Fransiskus – an interdiocesan agreement extended every three years. Romuald has only been here seven years, but already speaks impeccable Polish, with barely a trace of a foreign accent.
Upon arriving in Poland, he learned the language intensively – for seven months, from Monday to Saturday, seven hours a day. “I knew from the outset that if I couldn’t communicate well with the faithful, I wouldn’t build any relationship with them,” he says.
Romuald was born in the village of Kaza, near Sotouboua. His father was a French teacher in the local primary school. And so his first language was French – he only learned Kabije, the ethnic language in northern Togo, in later years. His family is Catholic. And their neighbours? A mixture, just like everywhere else in Togo: the majority are Muslims, but there are also some Catholics and followers of traditional faiths.
The proportion of people in Poland who are religious non-believers has risen to a record 14% while those who attend Sunday mass have fallen to a low of 34%.
But a large majority of Poles still identify as believers and Catholics https://t.co/2yqrLePAsw
— Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 23, 2024
The Mozou family are very religious. As a young boy, Romuald and his family would pray together daily, and this was what first brought him into indirect contact with Poland: every evening, along with his parents, two sisters and two brothers, he recited Saint Faustina Kowalska’s Chaplet of the Divine Mercy. He also associated Poland with John Paul II – to date the only pope to have visited Togo.
Romuald’s great passion has always been football. His dream of a professional career led him to neglect his studies, until his father made things clear: first school, then football.
While at high school, however, Romuald started to consider the priesthood. After taking his exams, he began studying in a seminary in Lomé, the Togolese capital. Three years in, the bishop proposed that he go to Poland to study at the seminary in Opole.
A growing number of Poles are turning away from the Catholic church, but not from religious belief itself.
This creates challenges for the church, but also for Polish identity, which has historically been linked to Catholicism, writes Katarzyna Skiba https://t.co/udWGzd0X7F
— Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) April 18, 2023
As a dean, Father Romuald gained hands-on experience in Krapkowice. After his ordination in May 2024, he became a curate in Opole (and from August this year he will be based in nearby Ujazd). I ask him how the new parishioners responded to him.
“Well, to be honest, they were a little surprised at first,” he laughed. “But that’s hardly surprising – after all, I’m the first priest from Africa to serve in the Opole diocese. They gave me a very warm welcome, though – I’ve never encountered any unfriendly gestures or words from them.”
In Poland, Romuald’s childhood passion has been rekindled: he’s playing football again. First for Maciowakrze, a club playing in Klasa B (the eighth tier of the Polish league system), then in Żywocice, in Klasa A. He now plays as a striker for GKS Piomar Tarnów Opolski-Przywory.
“I don’t know if I’ll return to my homeland – everything is possible,” Romuald says. “I feel good in both Poland and Togo.”
Polish dioceses recruiting in Africa
In 2026, 196 priests are to be ordained in Poland – 12 fewer than last year and some 205 down on the figure from 2013. The number of dioceses in which no ordinations took place because of a lack of candidates is growing – seven this year, compared to six in 2025.
“We actually have a vocations crisis everywhere in Europe, so we will be looking for priests in other parts of the world,” says Andrzej Kobyliński.
“Essentially, we have two areas where we can recruit candidates for the priesthood. Mainly Africa, and possibly India, but the experiences of German and Italian dioceses show that priests from India find it harder to settle in Europe.”
“Latin America is not an option, as the Catholic church there is facing its own crisis of a mass exodus to Pentecostal churches,” he adds. “So in the future we will definitely be working intensively with African dioceses. This is an enormous historical change, because it was once Poland and Europe that sent missionaries to Africa.”
One of the lads
Przywory, a village near Opole, the GKS Piomar Tarnów Opolski-Przywory home pitch. Seven p.m. Training has started. Father Romuald Mozou is a little late, so he rushes into the dressing room.
“Romek, you’re doing push-ups as punishment,” laugh his teammates when he appears on the pitch.
Everyone calls him by this Polish diminutive – Romek. The team’s coach, Marcin Chudala, admits that the players like to have a laugh at the footballing priest’s expense. “Sometimes we joke when he’s sitting on the bench staring at his phone: ‘What are you doing, Romek – confessing?’ The banter can be cruel,” says the coach.
But he also admits that Romek’s presence has left its mark on the team. Less swearing, for example. Even if there is nothing to suggest that Romek is a priest.
“We treat him just like one of the lads from the playground,” Chudala says.

title: Kojonup star Sheridan Kowald recognised as Katanning Netball Association A-grade player of the year
content:
Katanning Netball Association celebrated its top players, umpires and volunteers of the 2026 season at its annual awards night last month.
The Katanning Leisure and Function Centre hosted players, coaches, umpires and club officials for an evening of celebration on August 29 after a hugely competitive season across all the senior grades.
Kojonup shooter Sheridan Kowald took home the biggest award of the night as she was named best and fairest in the A-grade competition after a stellar season with one of the top teams.
Allstars’ Lara Rodney also polled well all season, coming in as runner-up in a tight count.
Rodney also took home the award for most improved junior playing in the senior competition, reflecting a season of hard work amongst experienced players.
Teammate Joshiquwa Wynne took home the coaches’ award after a consistent season as one of Allstars’ best defenders.
Kojonup’s Amy Williams took out the top gong for the A-reserve competition, with Allstars’ Jannali Seelander and Olympians’ Jaime-Lee Flugge finishing as joint runners-up.
Sandra Clues won the B-grade fairest and best award, while Kia Ora’s Darci Kerei was runner-up.
In the C-grade, Allstars teammates Rosanna Woods and Penelope-Lee Kumeroa-Puru won fairest and best and runner-up, respectively.
Association secretary Kirsty Flugge was named volunteer of the year, recognising her hard work behind the scenes helping keep the association organised and running well all season, while Addison O’Neill won junior volunteer of the year.
Brenna Schloithe took home the senior umpire of the year award, rewarding her hard work and skill umpiring games throughout the season.

title: Water supplied across SCoR network 100% safe, says GM
content:
VISAKHAPATNAM
South Coast Railway (SCoR) has on Monday confirmed that the drinking water supplied across its network is completely safe for consumption. The confirmation has come following the conclusion of an intensive week-long quality monitoring drive, during which thousands of supply points across four divisions were evaluated against strict safety parameters under the Indian Railways Medical Manual (IRMM).
The technical drive evaluated drinking water infrastructure at 3,680 distinct checkpoints including Visakhapatnam, covering passenger stations, residential quarters, and railway hospitals. According to official performance data released by the zone, 100% of the tested samples satisfied the health and safety thresholds set by railway medical authorities, clearing all immediate concerns regarding contamination or chemical imbalances.
The primary focus of the daily testing centered on residual chlorine levels to ensure proper disinfection throughout the delivery network. Field inspectors analyzed 3,441 distribution points across the four divisions. All 3,441 locations met the required chlorination standards, confirming that the water supply retains adequate disinfectant properties from source to tap to neutralize harmful microorganisms.
To guard against biological hazards, health teams collected 211 water samples from high-density passenger areas and medical facilities for laboratory bacteriological analysis. Testing specifically screened for indicator organisms such as Escherichia coli (E. coli) and coliform bacteria. The analysis yielded zero positive tests for biological contamination, verifying that supply pipelines, overhead storage tanks, and station coolers remain free from sewage or surface runoff infiltration. Routine testing continues on a monthly basis for major facilities and bi-monthly for minor stations.
In addition, 28 comprehensive chemical tests were conducted to check pH levels, total dissolved solids (TDS), and heavy metal concentrations. All 28 samples fell strictly within permissible safety limits, ensuring chemical purity across both long-standing and newly integrated water sources.
SCoR general manager Sandeep Mathur noted that daily residual chlorine checks will continue uninterrupted alongside surprise inspections to ensure that water quality does not drop during seasonal shifts or operational fluctuations.

title: Na jaren juridisch gevecht: ex-Martinair-piloten kunnen tonnen aan achterstallig loon krijgen
content: De zaak draait om voormalige vrachtvliegers van Martinair. Martinair stopte in 2014 met het vrachtvervoer en de activiteiten gingen over naar KLM. De vliegers verloren destijds hun baan. Na een lange reeks procedures is vastgesteld dat sprake was van een overgang van onderneming. Daardoor hadden de vliegers volgens de rechter vanaf 1 januari 2014 bij KLM in dienst moeten zijn. Loon over acht jaar De voormalige vliegers hebben recht op loon over de periode van 1 januari 2014 tot het moment waarop KLM hen weer in dienst nam, op 1 januari 2022. Dat komt neer op bijna acht jaar aan achterstallig loon. De precieze afrekening moet per piloot worden gemaakt. Die hangt onder meer af van de functie, het salaris dat de vlieger bij Martinair verdiende, salarisontwikkelingen, vakantiegeld, pensioen en wettelijke rente. Ook kan worden gekeken naar inkomsten die iemand in de tussentijd elders heeft gehad. Daarom krijgt niet iedere oud-vlieger hetzelfde bedrag. Voor individuele vliegers kan de totale bruto loonvordering volgens een grove berekening oplopen tot in de hoge tonnen of rond 1 miljoen euro. Geen hoger KLM-salaris De vliegers krijgen niet automatisch het hogere loon dat bij de KLM-cao voor piloten hoort. De rechter heeft bepaald dat de arbeidsvoorwaarden die bij Martinair golden bij de overgang zijn blijven bestaan. Het achterstallige loon moet dus worden berekend volgens de Martinair-cao en de daarbij behorende pensioenregeling. Dat verschil is belangrijk. De oud-vliegers krijgen wel loon waarop zij volgens de rechter recht hadden, maar niet alsnog met terugwerkende kracht alle gunstigere KLM-voorwaarden. Eerdere uitspraak teruggedraaid In januari 2024 wees de kantonrechter in Amsterdam de meeste eisen van de oud-Martinair-vrachtvliegers nog af. De rechtbank oordeelde toen wel dat zij recht hielden op de Martinair-cao, maar ging niet mee in de loonclaim zoals die was ingediend. In hoger beroep kregen de vliegers alsnog deels gelijk. De kern is dat KLM loon moet betalen over de jaren waarin de vliegers, juridisch gezien, in dienst waren maar feitelijk geen loon van KLM ontvingen. Geen vast bedrag per vlieger De formulering dat alle oud-Martinair-vliegers 1 miljoen euro krijgen, is te stellig. Er is geen openbaar vastgesteld bedrag per persoon. Het gaat om een mogelijke maximale bruto-orde van grootte, die pas duidelijk wordt na individuele berekeningen. De groep bestaat uit ongeveer 250 voormalige vrachtvliegers. De totale financiële gevolgen voor KLM kunnen daardoor aanzienlijk zijn. title: 51,000 get govt job letters at Rozgar Mela; Modi urges citizen-first service
content:
51,000 get govt job letters at Rozgar Mela; Modi urges citizen-first service
Over 51,000 young people received Union government job appointment letters at the 20th Rozgar Mela, where PM Modi urged recruits to serve citizens with honesty and efficiency.
More than 51,000 young people received appointment letters for Union government jobs on Saturday at the 20th Rozgar Mela, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi urging the new recruits to serve citizens with efficiency, honesty and a focus on public welfare.
The appointments were announced through video conferencing at programmes held simultaneously in 45 locations. The recruits will join Union government ministries and departments, including revenue and financial services, railways, home affairs, health and family welfare, and defence.
The latest round takes the total number of appointment letters issued through the Rozgar Mela initiative to about 12.75 lakh, according to the government. Modi congratulated the recruits and their families, crediting their achievement to both their hard work and their families’ sacrifices.
Modi linked the recruits’ entry into government service to the goal of making India a developed country by 2047, saying they would play an important role in building a developed and self-reliant India.
He said citizens’ confidence was the government’s real strength and that an employee’s conduct could shape how people experienced the state. Pensioners, students awaiting scholarships and farmers seeking benefits, he noted, often encounter the government through individual officials.
“Your behaviour, your consistency, your efficiency, your honesty” would determine that experience, Modi said, urging recruits to remove difficulties they or their families may have faced while accessing public services. He also asked them to consider young people’s aspirations in administrative decisions and remove barriers to innovation.
Modi placed the government’s employment push alongside efforts to prepare young Indians for a changing economy. He cited the National Education Policy, Skill India, the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana and expanded apprenticeship opportunities as measures to align education and skills with industry requirements.
He highlighted the PM-SETU programme, under which 1,000 government industrial training institutes are being modernised with an investment of ₹60,000 crore and greater industry participation.
He also said half of India’s recognised startups are located in tier-2 and tier-3 cities, reflecting growing participation from smaller towns in entrepreneurship and job creation.
Modi said the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana, with an allocation of about ₹1 lakh crore, would support new employment opportunities, including incentives of up to ₹15,000 for first-time workers. The scheme is expected to benefit around two crore young people entering the workforce for the first time.
He cited India’s 7.8% growth rate in the first quarter of the current financial year and an investment increase of about 12% as signs of economic momentum. He also referred to free trade agreements with around 40 countries, saying they could open markets and partnerships for Indian entrepreneurs and create new career opportunities.
Modi said adapting to technology and continuing to learn would be essential for improving public administration. Referring to Mission Karmayogi, he said more than 1.7 crore government employees had joined the Karmayogi platform, which offers programmes to upgrade skills and build familiarity with emerging technologies and systems.

title: Minsa: más de 200 peruanos recibieron trasplante de médula ósea en el presente año
content:
El Ministerio de Salud (Minsa) informó que más de 200 pacientes recibieron un trasplante de médula ósea en lo que va del 2026, como parte de la atención especializada que brinda el sector para el tratamiento de enfermedades de la sangre como leucemia, linfomas, mieloma múltiple y otras patologías hematológicas.


A través de la Dirección General de Donaciones, Trasplantes y Banco de Sangre (Digdot), el Minsa viene fortaleciendo la atención de pacientes que requieren este procedimiento, que se realiza en el Instituto Nacional de Salud del Niño San Borja (INSN-SB), el Instituto Nacional de Enfermedades Neoplásicas (INEN) y el Hospital Nacional Dos de Mayo (HNDM), de acuerdo a las características y necesidades de cada paciente.
En el marco del Día Mundial del Donante de Médula Ósea, que se conmemora cada tercer sábado de septiembre, el Minsa destaca la importancia de fortalecer la donación de células progenitoras hematopoyéticas, debido a que la posibilidad de realizar un trasplante depende, en muchos casos, de encontrar un donante compatible.
Las células progenitoras hematopoyéticas son las encargadas de producir los diferentes componentes de la sangre. Cuando el tratamiento requiere células de otra persona, la compatibilidad se determina principalmente mediante características biológicas, por lo que no todos los donantes son compatibles con todos los pacientes.
Una nueva oportunidad
Es importante precisar que la donación de médula ósea no significa donar médula espinal ni implica una intervención en la columna vertebral. Las células progenitoras hematopoyéticas pueden obtenerse mediante diferentes procedimientos, de acuerdo a la evaluación médica y las características del donante.
El trasplante puede realizarse entre familiares cuando existe compatibilidad, aunque también puede requerirse la búsqueda de un donante compatible no familiar.
De esta manera, el Ministerio de Salud continúa fortaleciendo la atención de pacientes que requieren este tipo de tratamiento y promueve acciones que permitan ampliar las posibilidades de encontrar donantes compatibles y brindar una oportunidad de vida a quienes enfrentan enfermedades hematológicas.
